As a skin prep or primer for costume make up this worked great and help up (I did use Mehron setting spray as well, however).  However the claim that it stops sweating doesn’t really hold true.  While applying my make up, as I sprayed it on a bit somehow hit my lip and part of tongue which instantly felt like the desert and tasted like I licked a deodorant stick lol.  So I thought all would go to plan.  And it did a great job of making my skin feel normal but keeping me from sweating during make up application and up until I got to the show and it was extremely hot and humid.  I don’t feel like I was sweating any less than would be normal and I was having to pat myself down with a towel constantly when I wasn’t onstage.  Also of note, the setting spray is meant to be cooling, which all setting sprays are, but is also meant to almost eliminate sweating.  I reapplied the setting spray several times just to cool off.  Still. Even though in was in the extreme heat and humidity of South Florida, where I wouldn’t expect anything to really stop sweating, I didn’t feel like my face was sweating any less than it would have been with nothing on my face.  HOWEVER… at the end of the night, despite sweating and blotting with a towel constantly, I was the only cast member who didn’t look a mess.  It definitely worked far beyond what I think setting spray alone would have done.  I’ve never used the mehron setting spray that but I’ve never had a setting spray of any brand work to THAT degree.  Stage make up is heavy and it still looked pretty great.  After removing my make up, my skin wasn’t at all dry either.  I don’t know how moisturizing it was but for a product that’s meant to be an antiperspirant, it was definitely not drying in the least.  So I don’t feel like it actually inhibits sweating.  However it’s an impressive primer and for stage make up nothing has ever worked better for me.  I have to keep in mind that I was also using mehron’s setting spray which I say the same about.  Didn’t affect sweating.  But held up.

There is a digital temperature display that shows the current temperature, which is a really helpful feature. There is also a power button, up/down temperature control, and a barrel lock to keep the clamp closed.

I did find that this straightener heated up really quickly. It did not, however, straighten my hair very efficiently. I had to go over really small sections multiple times to achieve the desired results. That cannot be good for your hair and it took forever! My hair is very thick and on the coarse side so it may be much better suited to someone with finer hair. Overall, this is a definitely a decent straightener but it just didn’t work well for me.

I ended up switching my moisturizers just three days ago to Bee Naturals Best Oil Free Moisturizer for both my day (with sunblock - Blue Lizard - Australian Sunscreen Face Daily Moisturizer Fragrance Free 30 SPF) and night time moisturizer (by itself), and this has worked out ten times better for me. Instead of waking up each morning discovering new cystic acne bumps and a scattering of blackheads all over my cheeks, or using 2-6 oil blotting sheets during the day, my face has felt clean yet moisturized, and I think my acne-prone skin is finally getting better!

In summary, I think AquaTica Organic Botanical Night Cream is fine and can be good for a lot of people, but it wasn't the game changer for me -- I have eczema, I'm pregnant, I have acne-prone skin already that's gotten worse since pregnant, and my face is generally oily. I don't think it made things worse, it moisturized, the scent didn't bother me, and it did make me feel better that I was using something natural, but it didn't make my skin noticeably better, especially because I still broke out.

If you look at the photo attached you’ll see that the package has a spot that reads “Don’t be put off by the pungent odour! It’s just the strength of the Valerian Root. (It disappears when in hot water).”

I believed that message. I should not have believed that message. It smelled like old gym socks left in a locker for a year and, while the taste was not as bad as the odor (or odour, if you’re Australian) it wasn’t very pleasant either.

As a food scientist/chef I always look back at my mentor telling me “It ain’t nutrition until it passes the lips”. It doesn’t matter how healthy something is, if someone won’t eat it or drink it, it can’t do them any good. Taste matters.

Taste is subjective and you may not be offended by the taste, I was.
As for its effectiveness, I can’t really say. There is literature that backs up to some extent, the claims made and it very well may help calm you or help you get to sleep. Then again, the same can be said for a cup of warm decaffeinated tea. Perhaps this is better than that but I’m not drinking it.

The packaging is very nice, it would make a nice gift for someone who is into this type of product. The painted glass jar is nice as well (the cap is plastic).

For what this costs, they should have at least used better tea bags; asking that the bags have strings w/ tabs on them, or that they are made of a higher-grade paper, shouldn’t be too much to ask when a teabag costs more than $1.00 per.

Again, the taste is subjective, you may like the flavor or, at least, not find it offensive as I did.

These patches work as well as other patches I've tried. They are not a miraculous cure-all, but they do help flatten out the acne and draw out the stuff that needs to be drawn out (don't want to get too gross and graphic here). They are small (1 cm diameter) so the coverage is limited, but they adhere well.

There are a couple of cons with these that lower my score:

> They are harder to peel off the backing than others, and it's easy to fold over the edge of the patch when removing it, making it less effective. Other brands I've used have slits in the backing material, making it much easier to dispense a patch without damaging it.

> The packaging is very wasteful. Each sheet of 20 comes in its own box. You could easily fit several sheets into one box. Either the box should be made much smaller or each box should hold multiple sheets. There's no need for all this packaging waste.

Three stars (average). While these work as well as other patches, there are other options that are better choices.

We gave this 3 test uses for an initial assessment of this back scrubber/brush. It is designed nicely, with handles that make usage very user friendly. If they made this out of elastic, you could shower and do resistance band exercises. hehe. Seriously, the handles work well, and act as convenient loops to hang the device to dry out in the shower.
There is an issue with using silicone brush heads, they tend to be soft/flexible. So, if you use this brush, do not expect the same experience as a loofah or bristle brush. And, you have to really work up a lather in your hands and then transfer it to the silicone brush head. Attempts to create foam/lather by rubbing body wash or soap on the silicone just wasn't satisfactory.
As mentioned, the brush surface tends to be soft/gentle. The 'scrubbing' side does rub, but nowhere near deep cleaning or exfoliating level. The bumpy side, for massage, does provide a textured rub, but is even less effective for soaping and cleaning your back.
Maybe I'm too old school, liking my cleaning brush to be able to really scrub.
Attached are photos to show real world images, with a ruler for size reference.
Did not use the included hooks, because we used the shower caddy that already had hooks for shower accessories. The bonus bath sponge looks fine, but did not use that yet. Again, maybe I don't pamper myself enough while showering. haha. If the significant other uses it, any pertinent information will be added to this review. However, I think the majority of people will be concerned about the effectiveness and quality of the back scrubber.
So, the product does match the description and depiction in the product details. However, my opinion is the softness of the brush hinders the effectiveness as a shower back scrubbing device. I do like that it is very resistant to mold and is extremely easy to clean and maintain. Maybe I have to learn to adapt to the softer texture of this type of brush. Based on our experience, this silicone brush garners a 3.5 rating. If you already use and like silicone back scrubbers, this is a quality product worth considering. If you are old school, this might disappoint expectations.

This comes in an outer product box that is inside a sealed plastic bag. It is made in the US. The ingredients are listed. The product box says that this is “80% organic. Made with organic ingredients, cruelty free.”

This claims to be a moisturizing lipstick. That sounds great to me, because I hate the feeling of my lips being dry at all. It claims to be highly pigmented, and have lasting color. It also said it has a vanilla fragrance.

I liked that it’s made of 80% organic ingredients, and it also had botanical extracts and essential plant oils. Looking at the ingredients, there’s some great ones like castor seed oil, sunflower seed oil, Shea butter, cocoa seed butter, jojoba seed oil, coconut oil, and vitamin E.

The tube is plain matte black with the brand logo on the cap. It has some weight to it. It kind of feels like it’s metal, but when I pull the cap off, the cap feels like plastic. The bottom part where you twist the lipstick is the part that feels like metal. It’s also the part that has the weight to it. But I’m not sure if it really is metal or not. The cap pulls off. It goes onto the bottom part really snugly, so I don’t see it coming off accidentally.

I got the shade “Crazy For You.” The product photo swatch made it look like a pretty medium pink color that had maybe a little peach color to it. It looked really pretty! I don’t think the color matches the product photo swatch much. I still like the color, but it’s a lot lighter than the product photo made it look, and no peach in it at all. It’s a bubblegum pink color. It’s pretty light with 1 layer. I did 2 swatches - One is 1 layer, the other is 3 layers. Even with 3 layers it didn’t look as dark as the product photo swatch.

There is no vanilla scent at all. I found that really weird since the claims on the product box state it has vanilla fragrance and the last ingredient listed is fragrance. But there’s zero scent, not even a hint of scent. I don’t mind if lipsticks don’t have fragrance. I just find it odd to claim it has a certain fragrance when it has no fragrance at all! The formula is really nice. It’s very moisturizing. It doesn’t feel dry at all. So I agree with the claim that it’s a moisturizing lipstick. It lasts nicely on the lips, so I agree with the claim of lasting color. The color is pretty, but I wish it was the color I saw in the product photo. I wouldn’t say it’s highly pigmented. It has decent pigment. It might be the color I got, but 1 layer is light, and it takes 3 layers to get it to show up more.

Overall, I think it’s a nice lipstick. The packaging is simple but nice. The formula is moisturizing and the color lasts well. I don’t like that the color isn’t what I chose based on the product photo swatch. It’s not even close, aside from the fact that it’s pink. The product photo swatch is a medium pink color, with a hint of peach. The color I got is a light bubblegum pink. So, I’m taking 2 stars off for that. I thought about only taking 1 star off since I do like the color. But, when you choose a color of lipstick, you choose it for a reason (whether it’s a color you like on yourself, a color you want to try out, a color you like that you want in your collection, etc.). Whatever the reason for choosing the color you choose, you should get that color. I understand sometimes colors can be off a tiny bit when ordering things online. But the pink I received is way off from the pink I chose. Other than that, the formula is nice. If you like moisturizing lipsticks and don’t mind risking getting a color way off from what you chose, I’d recommend this!

After having had a 1/4-inch buzzcut for about 15 years, about 18 months ago, I started growing out my hair, which is now quite long and sits around the bottom of my ear. As a result, I've been using different types of hair products to style it in different ways and keep it under control. Given a chance to try this pomade, I decided to give it a shot.

Packaging-wise, this is really simple: a glass jar with a metal lid. It has that old-timey barbershop feel, and would look nice on your counter or shelf, if you're into displaying your grooming products. Just remember it's glass, and an accidental drop on your counter or tiled floor is going to result in a disaster. The lid is a good quality and the seal seems to keep the product fresh.

As soon as you open this jar, you'll recognize that "barbershop scent". It has that minty-eucalyptus odor that's refreshing and eye-opening. There are days when I use this, when I'm sitting at my desk I wonder "what smells so good"...and I realize it's my hair. So if you're into good scents and smelling-good for yourself or others, you'll definitely like this.

The consistency of this product is quite interesting. It looks like vanilla pudding. However, it's definitely much thicker than vanilla pudding. It's not sticky. It feels and looks like a compound that would end up very oily in your hair, but that's not the result. Even given my hair's length, I don't have to use a lot of this, and typically on damp hair I only have to use about two fingertips' worth of this product in my hair.

While your mileage may vary, when I put this in my hair, it has an immediate effect. It provides immediate styling strength. It also helps to add a bit of volume, so that as I comb it through, I can easily prop-up the parts of my hair to give it a little volume and height. It dries well and doesn't get too stiff, leaving my hair with some movement, where I'm not afraid to run my fingers through it or adjust it. I'd say it's really good for my more "casual day" styles.

My only complaint, and for me this is really important, is that it doesn't rinse well in the shower. I only wash my hair every third day to maintain its health, and while nearly every other product I use rinses almost cleanly without leaving much of a residue, this particular product won't rinse cleanly. This becomes a problem if I use this on day two, but want to use a different product on day 3, for example. It definitely adds to residual build-up. I realize not every product rinses cleanly with just water, but this one is particularly problematic, forcing me to either wash my hair earlier or plan the days on which I use this so the build-up doesn't become an issue on consecutive days. So, if like me, you don't like washing your hair often, this may be a deal-breaker.

Overall, though, I'm quite impressed. The small jar is actually going to last me quite some time. It has a great scent and styling power. I'd probably use it every day if it weren't for the rinsing issue.

I gave this 3 stars for "Softness" because the brush is average to a bit firmer than what would be ideal and comfortable to use on your back, while the loofah strap is average. The brush bristles are kind of scratchy and not the "good exfoliating" kind of scratchy. They're more like the "ouch, that's scratching me" kind of scratchy. Overall, though, it's acceptable and average.

Next, I gave this 2 stars for "Easy to use" because I don't find this easy to use. The brush is separate from the stick that extends it to reach your back; you slide the oval-shaped brush onto the stick by inserting the stick into a cut out section on the back side brush. The problem here is that it doesn't stay on firmly at all. I ended up with 2 options: either not on firmly enough, so it kept popping off, or pushed on so much that it's very difficult to get off of the stick to use separately. The loofah strap is really easy to use, though. It's nice and long so there's plenty of length to comfortably hold each end and move it back and forth at most angles, no matter how thin or thick your arms or body may be. That's a real plus! But I still couldn't give more stars if only half of the set is easily usable.

Finally, I gave this 4 stars for sturdiness because there's no doubt, it seems pretty sturdy. The bristles on the brush have stayed intact. The loofah strap is firm and sewn solidly -- but it may be too firm. It's hard to get flexibility out of it. The elastic strap handle on the brush is flimsy, but overall, it's a solid set. The wood is a good, solid, well-finished wood without splits or cracks. It doesn't seem like a cheap product that's going to warp and break easily if you keep it away from hanging to be soaked when it's not needed for use. Putting it somewhere nearby where it stays dry is best.

I'm an eyebrow fanatic, and I've used eyebrow wax, powder, pencils and stencils. I'm a huge fan of shaping and powder - that seems to work best for me - but I've never seen applicators like these so I thought I would give them a try.

Mine didn't arrive overly wet like those of other reviewers; they just seemed to be like normal pens. But the application was uneven and I did have to press hard to get any color other than simply a dark shading (like the side of a lead pencil).

Once I did use firm pressure, it was a little like using an old eyebrow pencil - but less forgiving with the multi-levels. Be sure to shape your eyebrow first, then apply the pen; don't expect the pen to comb as well as draw. The pen can provide the dramatically even look, or, with a lot of manipulation, a more natural look (which I prefer).

I didn't find the pen to be as long-lasting as expected. I try to be really careful in application, as I don't like to abuse my eyebrows or skin, and remove product only using makeup remover. However, I do perspire on my t-zones and that perspiration completely defeated the eyebrow pencil.

Braun's competitively priced electric powered toothbrushes are very good values and reliable performers. Most models use the same rotating type replacement toothbrush heads.

The Advance Power 4500PX Bright D4510, like most electric toothbrushes that use AA batteries, delivers significantly lower brushing torque than a toothbrush with a built-in rechargeable battery, such as Braun's Vitality model. The Vitality may cost a little more, but it delivers a lot more brushing power, and the high capacity battery allows for many uses between recharges.

Both Braun models will do a good job, however the faster more powerful Vitality, will probably get more done in the same amount of time. Given the small price differential, and long life rechargeable battery, the Vitality would seem to be a much better value. Those who prefer a more gentle brushing action, can go with the 4500PX, or any of the multitude of AA battery powered toothbrushes available.

First, I suggest to do one eye at a time even though it takes longer. You’ll be doing yourself a favor.

1. I would cut the lift pad to your eye size, it makes working with it much easier. Visualize how and where you want your lashes to curl and place it accordingly. I wanted mine to flare out a bit so I put mine a little further away from my inner corner so that my lashes on the outer corner had space on the pad.

2. I used the Tarte Micellar Water to cleanse my eyelashes. The glue it comes with is awful and weak. You can actually use any eyelash glue to glue down your lashes. I used the House of Lashes glue. I used this glue to apply the pads onto my eyelid. You can use the glue however way you need to to keep your lashes down. I used a spoolie to push the lashes against the pad and held it there for a few seconds then I used the Y tool to separate them. BE GENTLE AND SWIFT. If you’re too rough you might rip your eyelashes off and the longer the glue sits the harder it will be to separate the lashes.

3. When I was satisfied with the eyelash separation I applied the perm lotion. ONLY PUT THE PERM LOTION ON THE BASE OF THE EYELASHES. From the very bottom to the middle where you want it to curl. If you apply it to the whole eyelash, your adhesive will loosen and your lashes will start coming off the pad. I used a Q-tip to apply this. Also I place a small piece of cling wrap on top of my eyelashes after applying the perm lotion to further secure my lashes from coming off.

4. After 20 minutes, I delicately removed the cling wrap, I used another Q-tip to apply the fixation lotion. This is thicker than the perm and should be applied to the whole lash. But still be very careful and gently apply it. I placed another small piece of cling wrap on top of my lashes to secure my eyelashes in place again.

5. After 20 minutes, I gently removed the cling wrap and used another Q-tip to apply the nutrition oil to my lashes. Then I used another Q-tip to apply the cleanser that comes with the box onto my lashes. Gently free your lashes from the pad. I used the Tarte Micellar Water to remove the rest of the glue. I dipped my spoolie into the Micellar water and combed my lashes through them to get any more remaining glue off.

The lashes come out perfect! I hope this helps!

They foam up nice and the mesh bag provides a bit of scrubbing like I'd get from a standard shower puff. It's a bit tricky to use when switching from hand to hand as you have to try and keep the drawstring closed so the soap doesn't fall out but the drawstring is what allows you to hang the bag after your shower, which keeps it from getting sticky and covered in slime. The reason I deducted a star is the excessive packaging. The irony for me is that I got these to get away from buying plastic bottles (that can be recycled). Was pleasantly surprised by this product.  Decided to give it a shot, given I use men's facial hair coloring kits on a regular basis, and "Just For Men" is pretty darn expensive unless you can find it on sale somewhere (and even then it's still far from cheap).  Beyond that, the "Just For Men" light brown kit ended up leaving my facial hair looking more like a charcoal color.  Admittedly, this brand is certainly NOT a five-minute treatment.  In fact, I'm using it as I write this, and we're going on 20 minutes at this point.  But that's not necessarily a bad thing.  It's not irritating my skin whatsoever, and I like the fact that I can leave it on my facial hair and check it out every few minutes until it gets to the right shade that I'm going for ("Just For Men" was frequently "too much too soon", where I ended up with a much darker beard than intended).  As mentioned in other reviews, the instructions are printed on the inside of the packaging (you would need to rip apart the box and put on magnifiers to read the text), but as with "Just For Men", just use equal amounts of the colorant and developer in the mixing tray (which means, depending upon the amount of facial hair you have, most men with nicely-trimmed facial hair could easily get 3-4 treatments from one kit) and apply with brush.  If you've got patience and want to save some bucks, would recommend giving this a shot.

This allowed me to do it myself. The fact that they stick meant that I could put the film under each segment of hair, stick the hair to the low-tac adhesive of the film and have both my hands available to brush on the bleach and hold the rest of my hair away. Then I would calmly put down my brush and neatly fold the film closed. It worked really well and it was actually stress free! The adhesive is like having another extra pair of hands almost.

The only thing I found slightly less than perfect was that the films were just a tiny bit wide for the size of my head so I couldn't lay them out like the hair dresser does - a central row down the middle and sides. The see through film also allowed me to see how my hair was lifting. It was great.

I purchased the Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer a year and a half ago, so I now have some experience using it. Previously, I've owned two Panasonic trimmers/clippers. Both worked well for a number of years, but eventually suffered from the same problem; the battery lost the ability to hold a charge. When this happened to the first trimmer, I had the battery replaced locally; the replacement battery did not hold a charge as well. When the second failed similarly, I purchased the Norelco.

It was a tough decision to purchase the Norelco instead of another Panasonic. However, the Panasonic models readily available differed from those I had used previously and the Norelco had good reviews and a nice price. I was also a fan of the understated styling and Japanese build of the Panasonic units, so this Norelco was a bit of a departure. I don't recall the exact model number for the Panasonic, but something similar to the ER389K or ER205.

Overall it's served me well for the past year and a half. So, time to share my thoughts. The Norelco is built in China; I haven't noticed any quality problems as of yet.

Positives:
---------

Vacuum is a great improvement. It's much less messy to use this trimmer than those I used in the past.
Power is sufficient, even without the boost.
Battery (still pretty new) holds a charge for a long period of time and recharges relatively quickly.
Comb stays in position (one of the older Panasonic could switch to a lower position under pressure).

Negatives:
---------

It's loud. Bothersome enough for me that I put insert earplugs before using.
The circumference is large; it's a pretty large clipper. I'd prefer something more narrow.
Difficult to replace to guard if you remove it.
Brush falls out of small compartment in case (will be easy to loose it someday).
Possible for pressure to turn on clipper when in soft case; it's happened to me.
Gaudy looks. Why does it need shinny highlights?

This is a nice Nautical gift set with 4 pretty polishes.  They are 13.5 ml each, and made in the U.S.A.  Initially I thought I would love Stay Nude the most, but it ended up being my least favorite of the set, only because it is pearl and streaks are unavoidable due to the type of finish it is.  All 4 have a shiny topcoat built into the formula.  The 3 cremes are all very sheer formulas, not super opaque.  The thickness of the formula for all of these is good.  If you like a sheer formula, where you can see your nail bed thru the polish, then these are your jam.  I did several manicures with each of them, and found that if I wanted a sheer look then 1 coat worked perfectly, otherwise 2 or 3 coats for full coverage and less peek thru of your natural nail and smile line.  I did 2 easy coats for each of my manicures.  The blue (Hypnosis) seemed to have the best coverage, and the formula for that was my favorite of the 4, it dried the fastest at 8 minutes to the touch.  They all go on easily, with a regular round brush (not flat) and they dry fairly well, in about 10-15 minutes each layer.  I did find that using my own quick drying topcoat that these wore much better, but from the manufacturer neither base nor top coat are required.  I did not get any staining from these, which I love.  The pink and white will both be really good polishes for doing either French tip or pond manicures when you just want a sheer base, where you do a layer, do art over it, then cover it again, and more art on that layer-it gives a layered effect that is fun to do.  The color palate is a fun one, with lots of options for artwork.  These are not quick drying-more of the typical 10 minutes per layer, and I expected them to be hardened on their own, without the help of a quick drying topcoat, but that was not the case with them.

Impressive!  I've only had this product a few days and believe me, I received it in the nick of time.  I THOUGHT I wanted to switch from 10%/overnight to 35%/30 minutes.  I had no issues at all with 10% so I thought it would be quicker to bump on up to 35% and only need 30 minutes.  WRONG answer for me!  The second day of my new routine left my bottom teeth so sensitive, I had pain in my jaw.  It was like 10,000 bees stinging.  I immediately figured I had nothing to lose by at least trying this gel.  I put it in the tray and even though it was NOT instant relief, it seemed to calm the stinging down enough for me to get comfortable.  I fell asleep and after six hours, it was like nothing happened.  I got up the next morning and was able to eat and drink as usual with absolutely no stinging.  I will update this review after a little more time but the way it stands now, I won't be without this gel again.  I have a sensitive tooth in the very back of my mouth I am hoping to improve with overnight trays.  No noticeable improvement yet but it's only been three days.  Crossing my fingers!  **UPDATE**  After using this product for about 14 days (twice a day for 45 mins) I can tell a major difference.  I ended up bleaching at 15%/overnight which wasn't bad but I could tell it could have easily gone bad quickly.  An easy 30-45 mins with this after bleaching I was set!  I can also tell a big difference on my problem tooth.  It's not completely gone but much better. One small note (and it's kinda picky but......) The syringes can be difficult to "gently" push down and it's very easy to squirt out half of the tube without trying.  Of course, sometimes you can draw it back into the syringe but depending upon where it goes, you could lose it.  Like I said, it's a small thing and certainly not enough for me to never be without this for an emergency again!

I've used the Arcitec 1050 for about 3 months and like it with a few caveats. The shave is a good, close shave. Most days I shave as soon as I stumble out of bed at 4:30AM, without so much as washing my face. The shave is good, stubble starts to show by late afternoon. The days I shower first, 12 hours later it is like I just shaved. I am getting 25 shaves per recharge, better than advertised.

As stated by Norelco, it took several weeks for the razor to be really comfortable. May not have helped that those first few weeks were very cold and dry. I have used a Norelco for 15 years, didn't expect to need the 3 week break in, but I did.

I am not thrilled that the razor has to be washed daily, but it is easy to do. However, it means the razor sits open drying most of the time which is no real problem, but annoys me. On the plus side, after 2 months I poured a little isopropanol in the cup I got with Norelco cleaner fluid 15 years ago, stuck the razor head in it and ran the 1050 for 30 seconds. Much easier than having the take all the heads out and swish them one at a time as with my old 7825. The shave improved too, so periodic thorough cleaning is (as with all Norelcos) a must.

The trimmer is fair. It's fine for sideburns, terrible for my mustache. I bought a mustache trimmer, which works much much better than any razor's trimmer. So maybe that the poor 1050 performance was a good thing.

My one big concern. The first 1050 I bought died after 18 shaves. Just would not turn on. Would not charge. I returned it to the store and exchanged it, and the second 1050 has had no problems. But there are more electronics in the Arcitec than in my car. I suspect that caused the failure. So I am concerned about the robustness of the design. Although electronics tend to die early, or last a long time.

Oh, and the shape is the easiest I've ever handled.

Bought this on a whim after reading lots of reviews about silver/gray/platinum semi permanent hair colors. I applied this dye and didn't leave it on exceptionally long,  from start to finish maybe one hour 20 minutes.  The box says 40, but I read that some people left it on for hours.  Rinsing it off did not cause any staining in the shower as the color was not super dark.  I was pleasantly surprised with the mild color change when it dried.  My hair was shinier and the silver color changed the white to a nice shade of silver and the yellowish color was  95% gone.  Plus there was no awful smell.  I have had to wash it a couple of times already and I believe it is fading, but I am okay with that as I didn't expect it to last a long time.  I am now going to try the darker shade of platinum to see how that works out.  The photos I added of course don't truly show how it really looks, but it does make a color change.  I did make sure before I applied color that I had only washed my hair and did not condition or add any other products to it to prevent color absorption.

This is a review of the Silicon Devices 150W High Performance Auto Power Inverter.

I have this in my SUV to allow me to use my laptop on the go. My laptop I use for travel is older and has no battery that keeps a charge. It also charges my phone but that need is rare as my phone battery keeps a nice charge.
For those who may not know what a power inverter is, it is a basic device that you can plug into a dc vehicle outlet and converts it so you can use an ac device. (DC outlet to AC outlet.) This one does have an extra bonus as it throws in two USB charging ports. The USB ports are rated 1amp and 2.1amp. (Use the higher one for your tablets and heavy power hungry devices.)
This takes in 12volts DC and puts out up to 150 watts which is plenty for normal ac devices such as laptops and portable electronics. It is only 9.6 oz and measures 4.3” x 3” x 1.7”. It is made of metal and is very durable so you can toss in your glove or utility box so it is ready to go. Cable is also nice and long so you can reach from front of the car to the middle area so others can use from all the other seats.

Cons – One thing I did notice is that the DC plug did not have a fuse in line. The description indicates this has over and under voltage protection; however, I am not clear if this is for the usb ports and or if this applies to the ac outlet as well. Other inverters typically offer fuses or a fuse if you remove the end cap on the dc plug. (On the up side, the soldering inside the dc plug was very nice and solid with nothing loose or questionable.)

Tips / Notes – Make sure your vehicle is running when you use this. This has potential to draw a good deal of power if using the upper range of 150watts and can run down your battery if the vehicle is not on allowing your alternator to prevent battery drainage.

Summary – This works as described and is very small. It has a built in fan to keep this cool as it works. It is very quiet and does what is expected. I would recommend this to friends and family.

That being said, I used the serum on my face, neck, and upper chest, and used the cream on my neck and upper chest. I am used to having a pump for a serum, so the eye dropper left me unsure how to measure out a consistent amount to use each time. After a few days, I could feel a definite softness on my face, especially when I was washing it in the shower. (Remember, this result was from the serum only.) My neck and upper chest also felt softer and smoother in the shower. So I would definitely recommend the serum. As far as the cream goes, it feels nice and a did not have any issues for a few days. Then I got a light heat rash on my upper chest and made the mistake of applying the cream to the area before the rash had healed. (With the cream's active ingredients, it wasn't a good choice to sooth the irritation.) Today the area was still irritated, so I am thinking I will have to stop using the cream altogether. Again, check the ingredients to guard against any specific skin sensitivities you may have. I received this product at a discount in exchange for my honest review.

Overall, I'm fairly satisfied with my order of this spa set. The first thing I noticed is that everything smells fantastic! A strong coffee fragrance wafts from everything in this kit, and all three body products contain real coffee. The scrub was my personal favorite scent-wise; I find it smells just like a caramel lattee.

The body bar is nourishing and non-drying, but it is exfoliating due to the coffee grounds, so I wouldn't recommend it for everyday use. I do personally wish it was a tad larger, as it melts down quickly during typical usage.

The scrub is quite dense, as it doesn't contain added liquid. However, this means you get a lot for your money, as you only need to use a little bit on damp skin to get good exfoliation. I like the addition of almond and coconut oil, as it keeps it from being overly harsh, and makes it quite hydrating.

A little goes a long way with the bath soak. I love using it in a foot bath; It leaves my feet feeling nice and soft, and the aroma is relaxing and pleasant. It does dye the water a light brown due to the coffee, however.

I like the candle, but I'd consider it my least favorite out of this set. It has a nice burn time for its size, and it's in a beautiful black candle tin with a lid. However, I found the amount of scent it provided while burning to be underwhelming.

Overall, I really like this spa kit, and I think it'd be fantastic for any coffee lover. It's a little expensive at the current price, but if the candle was a little stronger, and the bath bar was a little larger, then this would be a five-star product.

I pre-ordered this deck months ago and after much anticipation, it was very well worth the wait.

I'm slowly going through the deck card by card. The packaging is nice,easy to take out without destroying the box. It also comes with a Spread Sheet. Literally. *snerk* A sheet which illustrates different spreads on the front and back. Very handy for beginners. The deck is roughly 2"x 4" and included are two extra quick reference cards -- one for the majors, the other for the minors. Nice touch. I wish all decks provided this.

My only complaint so far is they provided a 70pg. LWB. Nothing more. No large reference book with extensive background on the cards symobolgy, like they've done in the past with the Celtic Dragon and ShapeShifter decks. Kinda disappointed (hence the 4/5 stars). But if I wish to carry this deck around, a big book would be cumbersome I suppose.

HOWEVER, what is nice about the LWB is they provide a mythical background on the creature, a divinatory meaning, AND magickal use of the card. Nifty! Never have I seen the Magickal Usage option before in a tarot deck.

So, card by card, I'm taking in what I think the symbology means then reading the LWB and finding I'm fairly accurate. Either I'm getting
better at Tarot or the deck really syncs with me like the Celtic Dragon and Fey decks do (ShapeShifter is a more difficult one for me to grasp now, but I have faith in the future it will become quite the tool for me when I'm ready).

Lastly, and one of the reason why I love Lisa Hunt's decks, is the Wands/Air - Swords/Fire connection. Few decks represent that and I've always been more intuitively drawn to that way of thinking, even before my Tradition's teachings reflected the same.

If you are a fan of Lisa Hunt -- get this deck.
If you are a fan of mythology -- get this deck.
If you are a witch or tarot reader who is more connected to the Wands/Air, Swords/Fire -- get this deck.
If you are like me and need a reference card now and again (lol) -- get this deck.

Well, the first thing I noticed, and the first thing you'll likely notice upon using this product is how very watery or thin it is. As someone used to using thick, rich, creamy sorts of beard shampoo and conditioner, this was an adjustment. I would say this isn't a replacement for a beard shampoo + beard conditioner. But what it's great for is short-term travel. If I am going somewhere for a weekend trip, this is what I pack these days. Because while it's not AMAZING, and doesn't leave by beard feeling feather-soft, it's notably better than just using body wash on everything.

At home, I follow this up with an unscented beard oil after showering, and it makes for a very soft, very manageable beard, with a faint but masculine sandalwood scent that lingers the better part of the day.

As stated above, this is a beard wash, not dedicated beard shampoo and conditioner. As long as you treat it as such, you shouldn't be disappointed.

Like everyone, I was very skeptical about this cream. I've tried the nair, nads, sally Hanson, sensitive formulas, usually removes hair but hurts like a son of a b and leaves the skin red and irritated for hours if not days. I decided to try this out because of the reviews I saw on an ad on social media. I know, those things are worse than infomercials, but I'm a sucker. First, the instructions are not in English, but I've used enough of these to know the basic idea. I tried a bit out on my leg not so much for hair removal as I had shaved just a couple of days prior, but to test the pain level. After 20 Minutes, no pain, no redness, nothing! Granted there was also no hair removal, but again, you're usually supposed to have about 1/4" length for creams to be effective, so I wasn't surprised. knowing that it didn't hurt, I decided next to try my underarms. (Long weekend= lack of shaving, perfect time to try it out.) put an ample layer across my skin, waited 10-15 minutes, hopped in the shower, rinsed, and found it removed about 95% of the hair, again PAIN FREE! No black stubble, no razor bumps, just smooth skin. The hairs that weren't removed are shorter, so in another couple of days I'll give it another go along with the legs, but I'm thinking I may have just found my new best friend for the summer!

It does say not recommended for face or private areas, so I'm thinking it'd be a good idea to NOT give those a try, for those who might say screw it and want to do it anyway. I would trust the advice of the people mixing the chemicals to cause hair to fall out... just sayin'.

The razor is better than my old Norelco electric razor and the best electric shaver I've owned. I still have to pass over my jaw line and upper lip multiple times, but I have to do that with a manual razor.

The 9170XLCC shaves closer than my 12-year old Norelco, maybe just from having brand new shaving heads, and I have to pass over the problem areas less often: takes me 6 minutes to shave instead of 8 minutes (who invented the myth of the 3-minute shave?). I also had no razor burn and did not need an adjustment period, which I credit to my previous use of a Norelco shaver. Of course, every one's face and beard is different, all I can say is that it works very well for me.

As for the cleaning system, it seems like a lot of bulky equipment just to clean a shaver. I used it once, took over an hour, then had to rinse off the residue and wait once again for the razor head to dry. The cleaning cycle consumed 6 minutes of electrical charge (one less shave for me). It starts charging the razor if you don't turn the cleaner off immediately when cleaning is done (questionable design when they say you should only charge when the batteries are near empty). I'll probably use the cleaning system until the included bottle of cleaning fluid is gone, but I won't be reordering the cleaning fluid. You can clean the razor just by rinsing with hot water or by using the included brush.

Final note, the included case is no where near as good as my old Norelco case, which has rigid edges and stiff sides for greater protection, and more room inside for shaver, cord and brush. I'm keeping my old case and using it for travel.

I will start of by saying Bella and Bear is an incredibly awesome customer-oriented brand that goes above and beyond when it comes to taking good care of their consumers. I have been a member of their beauty club, which I highly recommend. I have struggled to leave this review but honesty is the best policy. Hopefully my honest review can improve future products and makeup brushes from a brand I love so much.
I am not impressed with the Kitten set. Many of my friends raved about the Kitten makeup brush set and how much they loved it. The case is very stylish and classy. It is nice to have a sturdy leather case for my makeup brushes.

I wish the brushes were labeled – a pamphlet was included on using the brushes and their purpose. However, I wish the brush handles were labeled like it is done by some high end brands. A general consumer with less knowledge about cosmetics or brush usage will fumble around trying to figure out when to use a brush. I like the pamphlet. I found it neatly organized but it’s a piece of paper. I have no idea where it ended up.
A lot of the face and powder brushes are too identical. You don’t need that many face brushes that serve the exact purpose. Give me an angled brush or a foundation brush – all of these face brushes had the same purpose and it seemed wasteful.
The fallout – oh Lord, the fallout. I always wash my brand new makeup brushes with mild organic baby shampoo and let them air dry. I tested this before and after washing – the bristles fell out, but no excessively, as I was trying to apply makeup. One bristle got in my eye and I can’t describe to you the horrendous pain that causes. I had to be extremely careful to take the bristle out without stabbing my cornea.

It would be a far stretch to refer to these brushes as professional grade. They are great if you’re a makeup newb or trying to learn applications. The eye brushes blend very well. My eye makeup looked great – powder and blush were hit and miss. I think this set has a huge potential but lots of room to grow and improve. I'm leaving a four star review because of excellent blending and the case is truly fantastic to have.

I was fortunate enough to qualify for a discounted or free makeup brush set through the Bella and Bear beauty club giveaway.

I have tried a variety of magnetic lashes with the eyeliner. I will go over what I really like about this product and what I wished could be different about this product.

1. With most magnetic lashes and eyeliner it takes the eyeliner forever to dry and the eyeliner stays sticky and it sticks to my eyelids which I have partially hooded lashes so this is something that dries faster that is a definite pro.

2. A lot of magnetic lashes the eyeliner is really shiny but I found this one to be more matte. I liked that. Another pro.

3. Another annoying thing with most magnetic eyelashes is I have to make a really thick line basically covering most of my eyelid (keep in mind my eyelids are somewhat hooded) and I did not have to make a really thick line with this eyeliner. I did not have to do a winged line either. So I appreciate that about this eye liner and lashes.

4. A lot of magnetic lashes the magnets are so thick that it pushes the eyelashes away from your eyelid making it not look very natural these don’t do that. So pro.

The main con for me is if I wanted to take the lashes off to readjust them then it takes all the liner off with it so if you do that I suggest carry your eyeliner with you. It does come with two so you can grab one when you’re heading out.

Another con is it takes some elbow grease so to speak to get the wand out of the container so putting it in and out it is a bit difficult. I don’t know if this is done so it doesn’t dry out or if because there’s not a lot of product in there so I’m not quite sure I’ve used it a couple times so far I do like the product but I’m hoping that it lasts.

Over all I love how many sets of lashes it comes with and how it dries more quickly compared to other brands.

I have seen a ton of social media posts about these poly gel kits and figured I would give it a try. I am not a professional at all and can barely paint my own nails. I watched a couple of YouTube videos before giving this a try and I didn't do terrible! Here are some pointers for those of you that are trying this out for the first time.
1) you need to have a uv/led curing light. You start with the clear base and cure it before applying the gel. Apply the gel and cure, then apply the top coat and cure.
2) thick but not too thick!- If you make it too thin, the tips will just bend and break off. You need to make sure that you are putting it on about the consistency of the plastic nail that you use to apply the gel.
3) Don't forget to fix the bottom of the nail tip before you cure. If you don't do this you will have a giant glob of hardened get that you will need to file down.
4) If you don't want an ombre effect, you will need to make sure that the thickness is consistent from the top to the bottom of the nail.
5) Have a few disposable nail files. The giant one that comes with the kit isn't my favorite because it is quite bulky. I used a few coarse nail files to really get the shape that I wanted.

The kit itself is nicely put together, I just wish there were directions with it. You will need to have a lamp, nail file, cuticle cutter, and nail trimmers to accomplish your finished nails which is why I gave 4 stars instead of 5.

This is my second epilator from Amazon in a year. I got it because it has a wet/dry option and an exfoliator attachment unlike my first, an Emjoi model. This one is definitely more gentle but also less effective. It takes more passes and more time than the Emjoi model.
You should know a few things about epilating before investing in an expensive model if you've never tried it before. Firstly, six weeks of smoothness is a total lark. It must be done once a week to avoid unnecessary pain and pee a boo strays showing as plain as day. I could even see using twice a week if you have to have really perfect legs, say in the summer season. My hair is light but thick and upkeep is a must. Also you have to exfoliate religiously to avoid nasty red bumps and even then you'll get them every so often. The brush attachment on this model really isn't strong enough to do this job and I have to use bath gloves most days a week. If I do experience red bumps I will likely develop a scar because I'm very pale. So this is to be avoided at all costs.
The best part of this model is the attached light. It's bright enough to illuminate strays so you see them before anyone else does. It is gentle enough for all over body and face use so you can save a few bucks on waxing if you can do the upkeep yourself. It will pay for itself in a matter of weeks. It takes patience and practice to use effectively and isn't really a better option than shaving in terms of the time commitment. It is cheaper though and less dangerous and can also take the place of waxing so it does make economic sense. The smoothness of shaving can't be matched by an epilator, even immediately afterwards so you have to adjust to that as well. One of these days I'm gonna do laser therapy so I can avoid all the stinking upkeep in the first place. Oh and mom was right... It hurts to be beautiful. Go into it knowing its going to hurt at first but your tolerance will increase, especially if you do it weekly.

I've seen these type of curlers around for a while now and had been curious to try them out. However, upon opening them, I was disappointed by the size. If you have long hair and a lot of it, one pack will definitely not be enough, as is the case for me.
I was confused as to how to put them on. However, luckily for me, my sister knew how to do it since she had seen someone else try out this same style of curlers, but from another brand. Since she knew how to apply them, I told her to try them out for me and let me know, because I knew I'd end up frustrated.
Here's her take on them: They are tricky to apply at first and it takes a while to apply them, so make sure you have something else to keep you busy while you do this. However, once you know what you are doing, they're no longer tricky, but they are still time consuming. It takes time to section out the hair, put the curler in, roll it up, and repeat. Also, it is best if you do this at night if you are someone who has a sensitive head and is prone to headaches from wearing certain hairstyles. I put these on at around 3 p.m. and wore them for the rest of the day. After applying them, I was lounging around and watching a movie. Since I was laying down, I didn't notice any discomfort. However, once I was sitting up, it wasn't long before I felt a tension headache coming on. So, I would say that these are not good for someone who is sensitive to pressure from hairstyles. They don't look heavy, but there is a certain weight to having your hair "pulled" into the curler which can cause discomfort. I decided to sleep with them on, and was able to sleep just fine, since I didn't have any of the curlers directly on the back of my head. Upon taking them out, I had some nice curls, but I also had some wonky ones. I don't know the exact cause of that (rolled wrong, hair not pulled in correctly, moved during sleep, etc). However, I still liked the results and the curls held up for me, despite not having using any curling cream, gel, or anything.
All in all, they're a good product to try out and they allow you to get some curls without heat styling, but they can be tricky to use.

Having fun with my first fake eyelash hobby! I decided to see what all the fuss was about with magnetic eyelashes so I bought this brand. It did take some practice and trial and error getting the liner on and when to put the lashes on. I learned from social media to do the opposite of what the instructions tell you. LET THE LINER DRY FIRST PRIOR TO APPLYING LASHES! That made a HUGE difference, bc I was getting frustrated when adjusting lashes and the mess when following the directions that come with these. Let the liner dry. Takes a couple minutes and to be safe I waited 3-5 min then used my finger to check if there was any 'transfer' of liner. That did the trick and I wasn't having to use my nails to scrape any residue of liner when removing the lashes. They do stay on, but do not hurt to remove with out the eye makeup remover (which I stopped using for the fake lashes-only use to remove liner from my eye).

So all in all, I like them. This is coming from a woman who has never used fake eye lashes and prefers no make-up at all BUT knows I look better with make-up (wear make-up for work, social outing, special events ect.) I picked up a travel size tube of the Colgate Optic to take on a recent 5 day cruise with my husband. I don't buy whitening toothpastes so that certainly wasn't my motivation in buying it - this was literally the only kind available at the drugstore at that time! Anyway, we went, we cruised, we ate and drank to our hearts content, and we did our usual brushing routine in the morning and at night.  We've been home for four days now (and have not been using the Optic as we used up our little travel tube) and for the last two days, I've been trying to figure out what the heck looks different when I look in the mirror. I finally clued in tonight - my teeth actually are a little bit whiter! At first I thought it was the ultra bright lighting in the washroom at work, but I noticed again tonight while brushing my teeth before bed. I'm quite amazed that half a travel size tube used for such a short time has actually made a visible difference!  Now, with that being said, I don't think this is something I would use as my permanent toothpaste for two reasons.  One, I have white fillings on my front teeth and I don't want to worry about them looking significantly different from the rest of my teeth, and two, my husband and I both felt a very minor bit of tooth sensitivity toward the end of our holiday.  Neither of us has felt that since we got home so I think the toothpaste was probably the cause of that. Given the results I have seen, I would consider using this perhaps every other day and just keep an eye out for any sensitivity down the road.  I am definitely one impressed customer!

Like a previous reviewer, I also received steamer in a box labeled "O'Hair Steamer," but that didn't bother me because all 3 of the models I researched appear to have the exact same design. There must not be an active patent for this device. It was delivered via USPS and arrived in perfect condition. The instructions read like they were translated from another language. I didn't bother with the diagramed instruction booklet, I found a YouTube video from one of my favorite natural hair vloggers, Nikkimae. She provided step by step video instructions on to assemble a steamer that looks exactly like this model. Make sure you have the tube that connects the bonnet to the base connected, as well a as the tiny plug that is located at the base of the bonnet, or you might get leaks. It took less them five minutes to assemble. It took about 3 minutes to start producing loads of stream.
Because the stem that connects the bonnet to the base is not adjustable, you can't adjust the height of the bonnet. Fortunately, the counter I placed mine on and the chair in which I sat provided the perfect height to allow my head to fit under the bonnet so the steam came in contact with all of my hair. I still had to wear a narrow elastic headband so the back of my hair could come in contact with the steam.
I used my favorite deep conditioner and after 20 minutes under the steamer, my hair felt soft and was much easier to comb and style. I like the results much better than using a heat cap for deep conditioning.
The unit doesn't fold down for storage like a bonnet style hair dryer, but fortunately, I have the space to store it fully assembled.
So far, I am very pleased with this. The jury is still out regarding durability, so my opinion may change over time.

I have been using this product for a couple of weeks now and I have to say I am pretty impressed. While it is definitely no miracle in a bottle, I have honestly seen some noticeable improvement. First, it does smell great. It has kind of a light fruity smell to it - almost kind of cocoa butterish smell. It is non-greasy and absorbs quickly into your skin. It's very easy to apply. It doesn't cause any reaction, like heat or tingling or anything. It just rubs in like regular lotion and that's it. It comes in this bottle with a pump on it. It does take several pumps to get a good sized area because it absorbs so quickly. That is probably my only real complaint - that it takes a fair amount to cover an area like my thighs and the bottle is not that big, so I am going through it very quickly. Also the bottle is very smooth and awkward to hold - I know that probably sounds weird but you have to hold it with one hand and pump with the other, which is fine for the first leg, but once the stuff gets on your hands rubbing it into that first leg and then you have to grab the bottle to get more out with the stuff on your hands, it gets all slippery and is frustrating to get out. The bottle is too small to use the pump without holding it, so once you use it on one body part, unless you want to wash your hands every time (in my opinion possibly wasting some of it) then it is a little tough to handle. That's not a huge deal though - more of a minor annoyance but still worth mentioning. Maybe the people who make it will read that and fix it moving forward.

Anyhoo, it really does work well. In the couple weeks I have been using it, I have noticed my skin being more smooth, slightly tighter and my cellulite seems to be less pronounced. I have only been using it at night too. I don't have time in the mornings and if I used it twice a day I would go through a bottle in 10 days. I do plan to order more and I would definitely recommend this product to anyone.

CONS: The way this attaches to our vacuum makes it inconvenient for dog placement. The Shark has a handle which can get in the way. A hose attachment would have helped with being able to brush from any angle. You also have to be able to hold the brush down manually. Which is great for easy release of fur to be suctioned, but can make your hand tired for big/ multiple dogs. A locking mechanism option would be helpful.

I bought an electric shaver because I'm lazy. I used a Mach 3 for about 4 years and then upgraded to Mach 3 Turbo blades. I got a really close shave (I go with and against the grain) and with the exception of the right and left parts of my chin, there were no signs that facial hair even existed there. But this would take me forever, and the last thing I want to do when I wake up is shave. So I decided to buy an electric shaver. I've had the shaver for about two weeks now. I was not very content with my first coulple shaves, but things improved over time.

Pros

- Gets very close. The left and right sides of my chin are still difficult to shave, but I get much closer than I used to.

- Takes half the time to shave.

- There is a little collection compartmant that captures the hair so I can shave in my room while my roommates are taking a shower.

- It comes with 9 settings.

Cons

- Its difficult to shave around the neck. I tend to cut myself a little whenever I try.

- The cap was annoying at first becasue it is difficult to tell which side attaches to the front. I ended up drawing an arrow.

- Cleaing and drying it is kind of a pain.

- Near the end of the battery life, the shaver kind of dies down.

Overall, I am satisfied with my purchase. The instruction manuel recommends changing blades after a year (they cost about 20 dollars I think). I think its worth it.

Ok, so I have bought these multiple times and have been very pleased. That being said, here are some important things to not before ordering;
1. I do my extensions myself, and they look very natural by the time I am done. If you have put in your own extensions before, these are very easy to install and the bonding tape is high quality.
2. My extensions generally last between 2-4 months before reapplication is necessary. I shampoo every other day and leave in a conditioner to keep them soft. I reuse the same extensions for two or three applications and they do not show much wear with good care. That being said, I often use high heat on my hair and they survive very well.
3. THEY ARE NOT TOTALLY HUMAN HAIR. I would say they are probably about 70/30 human and synthetic. I personally do not have an issue with this as they last very well. I have bought lots of hair extensions and most of them are like this unless you are willing to shell out major money. I've done a full head in these and never felt the difference.
4. They hold dye decently well, but will fade before the rest of your natural hair so be prepared for that about 2 months in.
5. THEY WILL THIN YOUR NATURAL HAIR. Its almost unavoidable. They will cause damage. Take them out carefully and give your head rest time between applications. I currently only have two (double sided) extensions in to fill out my volume because the full head for 4 months destroyed my natural volume. Apply at your own risk, especially if you have thin hair. And buy the conditioner meant to remove them as it negates some damage. Trust me it's worth it.
4. Overall would and have bought again.

Well, I finally bought one. The Philips Norelco Arcitec 1050. I have been a Braun shaving customer for over 20 years. I find I'm able to get almost as close as a blade. So, why bother with any other shaver? Well, I'd always been fascinated by the triple-head design that Norelco pioneered back almost 30 years ago. The last time I tried one was about 10 years ago, and I wasn't impressed. With the latest Arcitec design, I figured it was time to give it a try.

The Arcitec Models
===================
Philips Norelco makes so many different models, I can't figure them all out. However, the Arcitec stands out by having a very distinctive slender look, the triple head surface on a flat conical piece that is affixed to a pivot, unlike the "neckless" other models. There are 3 main Arcitec models: 1050, 1060, and 1090. There are also two suffixes: X and CC. I think the 'X' means there is no cleaning station, while 'CC' means a cleaning station IS included. You may see some models shown without either suffix--this is the same as the 'X' (before they changed their naming convention). So, why is there a cleaning station if the heads can be rinsed under water? Competition. Braun provides one now... and with the scented alcohol solution, the shaver seems "fresher" after the cleansing bath. So, Norelco had to keep up. But in reality it's overkill; don't bother with one if you're thrifty. Rinsing the heads under water works very well.

Essentially, here's the difference: The 1050 has only 1 indicator for battery recharge needed, the 1060 has several LED indicators showing how much charge is left, and the 1090 has an LED double-digit display showing how many minutes of shaving are left. Quite frankly, the 1050 is just fine. When the battery gets low, you've got about 5 minutes left before the shaver will quit. Even still, for every minute the shaver is plugged in, that is how many minutes of shaving you get. Plug the shaver back in for 5 minutes, and you're ready to go for your shave. So... although this "early warning system" looks cool, it's overkill.

So, onto the shaver...

Appearance and Design
=======================
Out of the box, it is a beautiful looking device. Very futuristic. Adorned in several shades of black, dark gray, and silver, with catchy real carbon fiber side panels and a matte rubber finish along the backside for good grip. The three silver shaving discs contrast the black theme nicely. The shaver is lightweight and the heads have a lot of flex to them. The shaver comes with a charging base that serves as a resting stand, which secures the razor magnetically--very tasteful. There is also a "travel pod" included that allows you to charge the shaver while it is housed inside it. Certainly, the accessories are more impressive than what Braun offers. It looked to me like Braun has met its match.

Then, onto the shave.

The Shaving Experience
========================
This Arcitec 1050 is rather quiet, compared to my Braun 8595 Activator. I watched a couple of YouTube posted reviews of the latest Braun Pulsonic 9595, and that shaver sounded about as loud (if not louder) than my Braun 8595 Activator. So... Norelco certainly wins the prize for most quiet shaver. Actually, the sound is a low drone... it gives the impression that the shaver is a slow, antiquated device. The Braun sounds Bold and Busy with its Bounding Buzz. But in reality, the Norelco is formidable.

So, I touch the shaver to my face. I hear and feel the nibble of whiskers taking place. I begin to go through the motions... cheeks, chin, lip areas, then the neck. It feels comfortable. The discs are gentle. I don't feel anything like the reports of "heavy tugging" at the whiskers. I make a full double-pass across my face, then check the smoothness with my free hand.

Eh... not enough. Still rough. No immediate advantage over the Braun. So, I make another few passes. I pinch and pull at my skin as I would with the Braun. I do two more passes and check the smoothness again.

Eh... not enough. Better, but not as close as the Braun. I continue... I probably ended up shaving about 2-3 minutes longer than with the Braun. I found that after using the shaver for a couple of weeks and getting used to how it works, I'm able to match the Braun in closeness. It just takes a little longer. But the trimmer on the Arcitec? Awful. There's this little ridge on the backside of the shaver. A side switch partially extends and activates it, a small bank of cutting teeth. It's hard to get a nice smooth line. When you encounter a hair with it, there's a rather loud "click" sound. The Braun's trimmer is about twice as wide and zaps the hairs effortlessly. Although the Braun is a louder shaver, the trimmer does not introduce much added noise.

I do notice something else rather positive, though: no whisker dust on my clothes. The Norelco captures the whisker debris inside the heads and keeps it there, unlike the Braun which will dump a bunch of it on you if you turn it sideways or on a downward angle. For people who like to shave after they've gotten dressed, that's good news for Norelco.

Parts Replacement
===================
Norelco recommends replacing the heads every 12 months. Braun recommends doing so every 18 months. The Braun Pulsonic series tells you when head replacement is necessary... not sure how this is done (number of shaves?). The Norelco Arcitec has a little "head replacement" indicator. The Norelco replacement heads are about 30% more expensive than Braun's Series 5, and 8000 series, although the new "cassette" system with the Pulsonic is about the same. So, cost of maintenance might be higher. Also, I've seen mixed opinions about how long they last. Some people have complained having to replace them at 6 months, while an acquaintance says he replaces the heads every 10 years--when he changes shavers! He was once told that the heads are "self sharpening". That sounds a bit unrealistic to me. In any case, I can't report the replacement time here just yet... I'll need to use this shaver for a while. But I'll have to give it to Braun for a longer time between head replacement and at a cheaper cost (because it is also said that you can get away with replacing just the cutter block, if the foil is still intact, which drops the cost by 50%... can't do this with the Norelco).

Conclusion
============
So, the conclusion? The Braun is better overall, but by a slight margin. The Norelco Arcitec 1050 puts up a very good fight. I really could use this razor in place of the Braun, day in and day out. Especially if the girlfriend is still asleep and I want to be super quiet. That's what impresses me the most about the Norelco--it is very quiet. And it is great about trapping the whisker debris (I shave before I get dressed, so it's not a critical factor in my case).

Which shaver do I prefer? Well, at the moment it's the Braun. It may be louder, but it has a nice weight to it and is easier to grip. It also achieves a very close shave in less time than the Norelco. I'm planning to keep both... and will alternate between them from time to time. If I need to shave and make minimal noise, the Norelco will be my choice. For travel, I prefer the sturdier Braun. The Norelco looks better on the bathroom counter, no doubt about it.

In the final analysis
---------------------
Appearance: Norelco
Accessories: Norelco
Quiet: Norelco
Cleanliness: Norelco
Charging: --tied--
Parts cost: Braun
Trimming: Braun
Speed: Braun
Closest: --tied--

Crest Whitestrips are one of the most popular among the store brand tooth whitening products. They were introduced to the public in 2001 and they have been satisfying customers ever since. They work by concentrating special whitening ingredients like peroxide directly against the teeth where they can penetrate the surface for a full thirty minutes. Repeated usage for fourteen days should result in significantly whiter teeth.

Crest Whitestrips claim that these strips can be worn and used any time and that, once in place, you can go on with your normal daily routine for 30 minutes while the strips have the opportunity to work. It is true that you can do what you want, but there are certain activities that are not easy to do with one of these strips in place. I'm one of those people who has a tendency to want to move my tongue around when a have some type of dental object against my teeth and more than once, I have accidentally pushed the strips out of place. The gel helps to hold them in place but they can still be moved with little effort. Also, if you start talking with a Whitestrip in place there is a chance that some of your words will come out a little funny- like someone who has had a little too much to drink. I have found that, for best results, I try to do nothing at all when wearing Crest Whitestrips. The best thing to do is read a book. The time goes by quickly and it makes it easy to forget the strips are in place.

Waiting for fourteen days is frustrating and it is possible that you may need a second treatment after the first, depending on how well you stick to your 30 minute per day schedule and how well the Whitestrips stayed in place. But the results should make you happy. At first I avoided Crest Whitestips because of the price and because of the product itself. Spreading liquid gel on the teeth seemed much simpler than having to wear an object against one's teeth. I didn't like the idea of hassling with strips so I avoided buying Crest Whitestrips and tried the liquid variety in its various forms first. I finally gave in and purchased Crest Whitestrips because I got tired of waiting for satisfactory results. And I did get good results with these strips. I followed the advice on the package and used the upper strips twice per day first, then the lower strips twice per day for the next seven days. This is a good idea because you can compare the shade of the top teeth with the bottom, right after the upper treatment is completed. I could see a significant difference as all those years of soda pop, coffee, tea, and other staining drinks were suddenly washed away.

Crest Whitestrips use the same chemicals that dentist's use to clean and whiten teeth, so they are safe if used as directed. They are designed to keep teeth white for six months after each fourteen day period of usage. They also come with a money back guarantee. In order to get the guarantee. If you are not satisfied with the results, you can get a full refund of the purchase price provided you have followed the correct procedure for a refund.

Crest Whitestrips work well, but like other over the counter whitening products, they only work on natural tooth enamel. They will not whiten dentures, caps, crowns, or other artificial dental material. If you have teeth with artificial surfaces that are badly stained, you will need to seek the help of a dentist or other professional to get rid of the problem.

Crest Whitestrips are a little more expensive than the liquid whitening formulas but Crest Whitestrips are also more effective. I am satisfied with Crest Whitestrips and I recommend buying a box for effective treatment of discolored teeth. They are not as thorough as the treatment provided by a dentist but all things considered, these strips are a good buy. They eliminate stains and return your teeth to a more youthful appearance in only two weeks if used as directed.

I've been using Bare Escentuals "Bare Minerals" mineral makeup since about 2002. I've tried other brands but till now I just didn't find anything I liked as much, let alone better. Lately though the BE makeup just hasn't been agreeing with my skin. I'm getting older and my skin is a bit more sensitive these days apparently. The one thing I never cared for with the BE makeup was their use of bismuth. Anything with bismuth it just makes my skin itch. I've been reading about the negatives of parabens too, and I decided I wanted to get away from that as much as I could.

BE doesn't have that but it does use bismuth, at least they did as of the last time I ordered a big kit. After perusing Amazon and reading ingredient lists I chose to try this kit. Mainly because of the fact that this makeup doesn't have any of that and reviews here already are mostly positive. Also because I liked the eye shadow colors in the trial kit. These are colors I'd use a lot so I didn't feel like I was wasting money on colors I'd never use just to get trials on everything else. The jars are about the size of a BE eyeshadow, a little smaller maybe. The brushes weren't bad but they are small. I put them in my purse kit. They're useful for that, but not for much else. But they're sturdy. They're not losing bristles and they seem fairly soft.

For the most part I like this makeup. It's about the same grind as the BE mineral makeup, feels a bit silkier to me actually. It smells about the same seems maybe a bit less noticeable, the smell. It blends as well, but doesn't feel quite as heavy. The finishing veil is good. I have combination skin and oil in my t-zone and it did a good job of keeping me matte all day. The foundation covers well and doesn't make my face itch at all. The bisque is okay but I don't think it's got quite the coverage of the BE bisque. I did have to use more of it to cover things the same way. I kind of wish this kit had come with sample jars of the colored concealers as I would have liked to have tried those combined with their bisque. I think it might have worked better with that combo. I'm admittedly at a point where a simple bisque concealer is probably not enough for me. I'm getting dark under eye areas and have some red I need to cover now and again.

Their "glow" mixed with the pink blush is my new blush. It's too much for me as a bronzer. I have very pale ivory skin and it just does not work for me all over. Just a little too much orange, a little too dark but it did work okay as blusher over the pink they send you. Combining both that gave me a blusher that worked well for me. The pink blush they give you is just way too light and frosted for me. It just doesn't show up at all. It was the one product in the kit I just did not care much for. I would definitely want a darker more mauve or cinnamon toned blush rather than this one. The pink on it's own is pretty useless. I had to combine the two or forget it. It didn't even look like I had any color on my cheeks.

The foundation colors are decent. Their Fair #1 is actually a near perfect match for me but I'd probably never use the Fair #2 unless it was combined with the Fair #1 maybe. My skin is never that dark, not even in Summer. But Fair #1 I must admit I like that one. It's hard for me to find a foundation that's fair enough that's not too yellow, but Fair #1 works well. Fair #2 is just a tad too dark and just a bit yellow for me.

Overall I'd have to say this kit was a positive experience except for a couple of colors being slightly off for me. I do plan on ordering a big kit but I'm also going to email them and ask if they might send a slightly darker blush and just the Fair #1 x2 instead since they're supposedly picking the cosmetics as they pack for you. Can't hurt to ask, and if they do then their "Fair" kit will work very well for me and I can see myself becoming a regular with this one. I did not expect this product to be as good as it is actually. It was a very pleasant surprise. I'm used to spending a lot more on the BE product. This is much less expensive and in some ways I think I actually like it better than BE so I probably won't be a BE customer much now that I've discovered this.

I have the T770 model depicted above, so I've been a happy user for nearly two years. In his review, Reuben gives good tips on the use of this trimmer: take your time when you use it and clean it out after every use. The first results in even trimming; the second allows the vacuum to work best. Yes, a few hairs will show up in the sink, but with one swipe with a damp tissue they're gone. The adjustable comb trims beard, mustache, goatee, etc., to any length a user might want. In addition to the trimmer, the mustache and sideburn clipper gives a precise and neat edge; to use it, just remove the comb.

Taking the T770 apart to clean the blades is easy; getting it back together properly requires careful assembly in good lighting and some patience. I wish Norelco would simplify the re-assembly mechanisms and process. But even that, since I have now mastered it, does not truly lessen my liking of this product. Nor does its charging time; the T770 holds its charge for around two months (and I use the trimmer 2-3 times a week).

Should I drop and break this trimmer, as I did with a previously owned Remington, I will replace it with another Norelco. It's been great to have said good-bye to scissors.
