If you are new to shaving with shavettes or straight razors these ARE NOT for you. There are many other shavettes much more suitable to learn with. There are no safety features. The blades must be pushed into the razor from the front, and it is a very tight fit because it has to be very tight in order to secure the blade in place. The blades are removed by using a flat object to push the blade back out. The Turkish razors are smaller than most standard sized shavettes, and the blade base is narrower than most shavettes. I happen to love them, and the price is right. They're cheaply made but rather sturdy. I use small needle nose pliers to gradually push the blade into place from the front, then refold the package the blade came in and lightly/gently push down on the blade against the blade wrapper on a counter to ensure that the blade in uniformly lined up evenly. I remove the used blades by holding the razor in place with one hand while using the blade of a small knife to push out the used blade from the rear blade edge.

Since I recently requested and started using a Gel Polish kit, I found myself in need of some gel polish remover tools, so I requested this product from Vine. This review is for: Nail Polish Gel Remover Tools Kit for Women with Nail Clip Caps, Nail File, Nail Remover Cotton Pads,Brush, 2-in-one Cuticle Scraper/Pusher.

First things first, I was surprised to come here to write this review and discover that I received no dispenser bottle as listed and pictured in the product description. Since this kit does NOT come with the remover liquid, you are going to have to buy some acetone. (In my state, you must be 21 to buy it.) Since this came with no bottle, I followed the directions on the acetone itself, and used a glass measuring cup in which to pour it. (This way if I didn't use it all, I could easily pour it back into the bottle. Note to self, buy another measuring cup!)

With that out of the way, this kit worked as described. I used tweezers and soaked the little pads in acetone and then wrapped it around my nail and applied the clamp. I did this to all of my nails at once, because my husband was here to help me with the second hand. If you have no one to help you, then you're going to need to do each hand separately. It is impossible to do much with these clamps on your fingernails. Once the clamps are on, you need to wait at least 20 minutes before removing them, to soften up the polish.

Once I removed the clamps I set to work scraping off the polish. It does NOT come right up like regular polish does, but if you've soaked them for 20 minutes, and you applied it in thin layers when you originally polished them, it's easy to scrape the rest of it off. Once you're done, your nails look pretty bad. It will be necessary to buff them out and then wash them and apply some moisturizing lotion because your nails and the tips of your fingers will be very, very dry.

I have heard some real horror stories of people trying to get gel nails and gel nail polish off, but this kit made it much easier and alleviated my fears. Other than the missing dispenser bottle, I'm rather happy with this kit.

First let me say: READ my review CAREFULLY to avoid an eyebrow malfunction like I experienced. Second, the tint works great!! Third, I’m grateful for the bike chain degreaser I still had hibernating in my cupboard, 20 years later. Read on:

I tinted my eyebrows thinking that it was OK to get some on the skin above and below my eyebrows and that it would wash off easily. After all, when I self-color my hair, the excess color wipes off my skin with no problem!! Ya, nope not true of this eyebrow tint. The excess wouldn’t come off!!! In hindsight, I had a very Low IQ moment. The instructions do tell you to test a patch of your skin before using it on your eyebrows. I didn’t do that. You should!!

After I washed the tint off and attempted to wash the excess tint off, I saw a female Groucho Marx in the mirror. I tried removing the excess tint with 3 different face soaps, then regular body wash soap, then baking soda, then toothpaste.

Tier 2: Shout with bleach, Comet spray w/bleach. Then Lysol wipes... moved onto nail polish remover. Then hairspray. But what actually did it was the 🚲 bike degreaser I use on my bike chain. Thank goodness because I was about ready to just dump an entire Costco-sized bottle of bleach on my face and let a higher power step in!!

Worth noting: it was an eyebrow tint product from Slovenia so it probably doesn’t have the same ease of removal standards as American hair color products!

Great product but just be very careful not to overdo it and don’t get it on the skin near your eyebrows!! Aim carefully at JUST your eyebrows!!

PS. I am sparing you a picture of my mishap...you’re welcome!! 😊🤣

I have extremely sensitive and dry skin.  I need moisture constantly but many of the drug store options either don't really absorb into my skin and leave breakouts which cause all sorts of other issues, or the product itself will cause inflammation.  When I was asked to try this product for my opinion I was hesitant because it can take a moment to destroy my skin and weeks to repair it.  I decided to try it out on my hands first.  I placed the smooth scentless cream on my left hand and none on my right.  It was light to touch but needed to be massaged in.  I only used about the size of a new pencil eraser and that was more than I needed.  After a couple of hours I noticed that my left hand still looked like I had applied lotion which was a nice change.  By the end of the day, the top of my hand and the skin at the base of my thumb were still looking good.  This was pretty amazing since I must have washed my hands a dozen or more times.  I decided to go with the face today.  Again I used about the size of a new pencil eraser and that covered my whole face.  It felt good and I did not feel like I needed to add any oil to my cheeks on top of it.  Its been a good 6 hours and they still feel like they did when I first applied the cream.  Also, no redness - that is a HUGE plus.  I am really happy I took the chance to test this product.  I like that it works well and that I can give it an honest good review.

A beard trimmer with a built-in vacuum to keep the trimmings from collecting all over your sink is a good thing.  So when I decided it was time to replace my Wahl Vacu-Trim, which needed new blades and battery, I was sorry to see that Wahl apparently no longer makes that model.  It seems that the only vacuum beard trimmers available at this writing are the two models from Philips Norelco.  Seeing a good price here at amazon, I sprang for the Turbo model, which promised a little extra oomph.  Well, the trimmer works very well.  Better than the Wahl, I think.  To my surprise, I like the look it gives me at the closest setting -- if I didn't know better, I would say it makes an old geezer like me look younger.  I haven't had the problems others describe with the length comb changing settings on me.  The nicad battery life is acceptable -- I get a week of trims on my full beard and moustache at the Turbo setting.  When you see the red light come on after turning the unit off -- figure you have one more trim at Turbo speed.  Then it's time to recharge.  The unit is a little large, but not unwieldy.  I will be interested to see how well the blades hold up to the "ever-sharp" claim.  No lubrication needed either!  I am deducting one star because of failings in the instructions and packaging.  The instructions never tell you which side of the trimmer to hold against your face, and the T980 works the opposite of most other trimmers and shavers.  Most others have you hold the side with the buttons and logo against your face; when you use the length comb on the T980, however,you hold it with the buttons and logo on the side facing AWAY from your face.  I wonder how many of my fellow reviewers have been using this trimmer correctly, given this unconventional orientation.  Nowhere in the instructions do they show a clear photo of a guy using the trimmer.  There are two tiny, hard-to-follow line illustrations.  Adding insult to injury, the first time I called Norelco for help, the woman rep on the phone -- adding helpfully that she had never used a beard trimmer herself -- gave me the wrong answer.  Further experimentation -- and another call to a male rep -- confirmed that I was using the trimmer correctly.  The other problem with the packaging is the dreadful plastic blister pack holding the trimmer and accessories inside the box.  Any package requiring scissors to open needs to be redesigned with more eco- and user-friendly materials!!!  At any rate, the T980 is the current state-of-the-art in vacuum beard trimmers, and I recommend it, the packaging notwithstanding.

For me, this little nail drill works very well. It's touted as being good for beginners, but I was really nervous about using it for the first time, because it came with absolutely no instructions. Yikes! I'd cut my nails down to nubbins, and have been wearing falsies, so I figured it was a great way to get some practice.

There are a few notes on the product listing about how to insert and remove the drill bits, so with that being all I had to go on, I just went for it.

As I had no clue as to which bits were for what job, I had to wing it. I tried two. The first I tried wasn't quite coarse enough, so I went with the larger, barrel-shaped bit, which worked well for what I wanted. I'd basically put on some stiletto tips, and managed to jab every family member at least once. I didn't want to completely remove them, but I wanted to take them down a bit and round out the tips. Once I changed the bit this drill did a great job.

It got a little warm, but didn't get too hot, and it didn't overheat and stop on me. In my photo is what they looked like right after I was done. I did go over the edges briefly with an emery board for the couple of rough spots left, simply because I'm not yet quite adept enough to get the perfect shaping I want, but practice is key.

It's for the same reason that I haven't yet tried the drill on my natural nails. I will, though, once I get a little more know-how under my belt. So, in summary, I like it, and it seems to be beginner-friendly, but I wish there were detailed information available on its use.

I received this nail drill free to try in exchange for my evaluation and unbiased review. Any opinion I've expressed is purely mine and based on my own personal experience using this drill.

I'm inherently skeptical of masks and scrubs. I firmly believe that nature provides us with a valuable top layer to our skin, and that ritually grinding off this layer forces our skin to constantly try to regain equilibrium and add more of the oils and blemishes that we're trying to rid ourselves of.

So when I look at masks like this, I look for things that sooth and *add* instead of extracting and *subtracting* from our skin.

I think this one is a winner. I think it's gentle and soothing, and I think this one isn't robbing our skin cells from their naturally perfect sebum.

I've used several Norelco shavers over the years and this one was the best yet. It charges in less than an hour, yet I found I could shave for a month on a single charge. Lotion packs last about 2 weeks, yielding a smooth, comfortable shave with no shaver rash.

After using it in the shower for 6 months, I began to notice that it was filling up with water. The display window showed a water line across the middle. I loosened the screws on the back and let the water drain out, but it was already too late, the insides were rusted to bits. The display window turned muddy brown and I could barely see the LED indicators. I charged it one last time and used kept using it. After that, when the charge indicator glowed red the shaver would no longer charge. The shaver was finished.

I called Norelco and they told me it would be covered under warranty. I shipped it off (at their expense) and used my old Norelco dry shaver while I waited. Eventually, a new Norelco 7735X came to my door. I called back to complain about the downgrade and they told me that it was an error, that I was supposed to get a new 7775X, but there were none available. I was offered a choice of a dry shaver, a set of accessories for the 7735X, or a full refund. I chose the refund.

Now with refund in hand, I'm getting ready to buy a new 7775X from Amazon. I'll just not use it in the shower. The fact that I've had bad luck and am still willing to come back to this product may be interpreted as a strong endorsement--with the caveat about using it in the shower. That's the only thing that keeps it from getting 5 stars.

Here are a few things to know about these.
You need an UV light. The set I had were dry enough that I felt that I could almost not use an UV light but the directions say you need one and I followed the directions with this set.

You will file the top of your nails. so that these stick better. I did that but just for kicks to see how well it stuck without doing that, I left one nail top not filed. The polish did not stick to that nail. What this means is when you take off this police, the nail underneath will be very fragile and will rip off. This earned them the four stars instead of a full five stars.

The other thing you need to know is if you have short nails (as I do) the little gold design in this polish will most likely get cut off. The gold design on the plain nails is right in the middle of the nail polish and unless you have long nails this will be difficult to put on your short nails and keep that design. For years I've had a difficult time getting a close shave and a shave with minimal irritation. I've tried several of the Mach 3 variants with little success. Against or with the grain the Mach 3 would miss random places on my throat (especially around the adam's apple). I quit the Mach 3 even though the shave was otherwise close because the irriation it left made me unable to make a second pass. My Norelco Reflex Action series left me high and dry. That's right, it didn't cut anywhere and left me burnt all over. Most days it looked like I didn't even shave.

Angered over years of horrible shaving, I decided I would treat myself for my birthday. I was seriously considering Brauns and Panasonic's high end razors but decided against it because there was no clearly outlined guarantee if it didn't get as close as I'd like. Norelco on the other had advertises their's quite well and after reading a few reviews, I decided (...) I would take the plunge.

Here is my take after using a dry electric shaver for the past 2 years plus a weeks experience with the 7735x:

Pros:
1. Gets darn close for an electric. Not quite Mach3 but more then satisfactory. It does miss a bit around the adam's apple but nothing I can't live with.
2. Leaves me with almost no irritation. In fact, I can shave 3 times a day with this thing if I feel like it! Very impressed on the combination of closeness and lack of irritation.
3. Very easy clean up - just run under hot water.
4. Nivea lotion packs are easy to load and administer while shaving. They also really contribute to the feel of the shave.
5. The shaver itself is well built and sturdy.
6. Quiet.

Cons:
1. Cost-Cutting abound!!
2. Cheap charging unit that does not automatically shut off after full charge is reached!
3. Ni-Cad batteries.
4. Cheap Strap for letting the shaver hang out and dry.
5. Cheap/useless carrying case.
6. The shaver's "cap" falls off too easily.
7. Norelco recommends you run the shaver to empty before recharging. This can be a big problem if the battery runs dry and you need to shave - there's no way to plug the shaver into the wall and use it.
8. I can't for the life of me (and after reading the instructions 5 times) figure out how to get the shaving head off to put the trimmer attachment on.

Despite its near endless line of drawbacks, you do get a good shave with the 7735x. I couldn't stop rubbing my neck and face after the first shave (and it seems the shave gets better the more I use it). Oh yeah and the shocking part, I look forward to getting up at 6am just to shave! Yeah!

This "facial kit" has all the items you'd expect to get in a spa gift basket, only it's shipped in a cardboard box reminiscent of subscription boxes. The main difference is that it's a one-time deal, no subscription needed, and all the items are grouped together by theme and color. I ordered the "gold" theme and was a little disappointed that not all the items are gold colored (the eye mask is blue) and there's a mix of drugstore items with some more luxurious feeling ones.

I'll start with the good. The box is very cute, with the words "It's a great day to love your face" greeting you when you open the box. Inside you get a five count box of sheet Masks that contain retinol, a generous and thick box of facial wipes, a Gold under-eye pad to reduce lines and puffiness, and a gold Lip Mask (I've never used a "lip mask" before so this seems a little bizarre, if fun). The blue eye mask is filled with gel beads so you can use it hot or cold, and the cheapest and least impressive items are the "facial buff" (a pear-shaped sponge that looks like something you'd clean your pots with) and a "facial cleansing brush" that looks a little cheap but is nevertheless useful.

The main thing that was missing was some packing peanuts or confetti, as the items were tossed into the box hither and thither with NO padding, whereas other gift baskets and boxes typically include some stuffing so that the items are more artfully displayed. This one wasn't, so if I were giving this to someone as a gift, I'd certainly add it so the items wouldn't arrive in a jumble. But otherwise, I liked it.

I've been looking for an electric shaver for a while because honestly I've just gotten old and lazy and I hate shaving in the shower. I haven't used an electric shaver in years because none ever shaved that close and we're a total waste of money. I had looked at tons of shavers, a few epilators and shaver/epilator combos from the big name brands to the not so known ones. Many had a lot of negative reviews and several were way overpriced. After hours of research on Amazon and YouTube I was about to give up when this little gem appeared in my suggestions on Amazon. Reading reviews on this one I decided what the heck I'm going to get it. I received it today, just a little while ago, and it was already charged up and ready to go. I immediately tried out the shaver attachment and oh my gosh! I can't believe how close this thing shaves!

The key to getting a close shave is exfoliation. I regularly exfoliate so I always get a close shave no matter how I do it. Also the angle of the shaver is important. If the hair is longer tilt a shaver more so the trimmer can shorten the hair. Then hold the shaver more upright to allow the foils to perform the close shave. Go against the direction that the hair grows, use light pressure and make a couple of passes. It sounds like a lot of work and time but it really isn't. It's really convenient, quick and easy.

I haven't tried the epilator yet because I tried out the shaver part first so now I have to wait for the hair to grow back.

So far, I have no real complaints about this NIRA Skincare Laser & Hyaluronic Acid Serum Bundle. I’m still at the point where I’m not sure if I can say it truly works because I need to use it for a longer period of time, but I’ll discuss various aspects about the product that will hopefully help with your decision-making.

-Came well-packaged in a small, but sturdy cardboard box. Everything arrived intact. I have continued to use this box for storage of the product.
-Comes with the handheld laser device, charger with base to plug into an outlet, and manual
-No complaints about the battery life so far
-Simple to use: there are two buttons: The power button that turns the device on. Then you can press it to cycle through the various levels of intensity 1-5 which are clearly shown using green light bars. You can then hold the power button down to turn the device off again. The top button can be pressed to activate the laser after you have chosen the level of intensity you want.
-The laser only works if positioned correctly over an area of skin. It will give a single negative sounding beep if not positioned correctly, and a positive sounding double beep if it is positioned correctly as the laser works. You wait to move the device to the next area after you hear that second beep indicating that it is finished with that laser sequence
-The device has a white, plastic outer shell. It is lightweight while still feeling sturdy and durable. I would still be very careful not to drop this as I’m not sure how it could handle a fall
-I would recommend experimenting on the lower intensity settings. The undereye area is pretty sensitive. I feel I have a pretty high pain tolerance, but my eyes often still tear up after using per instructions on the highest settings of 4 and 5. For whatever reason, my left eye is much more sensitive to this.
-I don’t want to say it is truly painful, but I suppose the best way to describe the sensation is almost similar to if you were being stung by a rubber band that you pulled back and let hit your skin if that makes sense. It isn’t comfortable, but you do get more used to this and can work your way up to a higher level of intensity. You will probably also feel some warmth on the skin after using.
-I know this is marketed for under the eyes, but I have also been using on my forehead and by my smile lines.

***The instruction manual is pretty clear and straightforward. You definitely need to read this before getting started. Here is some information that you can find within the manual:

-They say all skin tones and anyone over the age of 12 can use NIRA to reduce the appearance of wrinkles around the eyes
-You need to clean and dry your face just prior to using NIRA
-It can be using morning or night and up to twice daily. They recommend waiting 1 minute before retreating each area and not to treat more than twice within a 1-hour period.
-Do not treat the same spot twice in a row, even if the pulse is rejected and you get the low pitched, negative sounding beep
-The instructions clearly show you the recommended way to treat the undereye area and the treatment pattern to use
-They recommend using the highest power level where you feel warmth without pain
-You should use a facial moisturizer after each treatment and a daily sunscreen with at least SPF 30 is recommended. This bundle includes the hyaluronic acid serum which can also be used.
-Device should be kept clean and free of dust, especially the glass lens which can be cleaned with a cotton swab. Surfaces can be cleaned with 70% alcohol solution between each use.
-They say some potential side effects include: skin warmth, redness, and stinging. Less frequent side effects include dryness, roughness, tanned appearance to skin, swelling, flaking, itching, crusting, bruising, pimple-like rash, irritated skin, blistering, scarring, infection, and skin color changes where your skin may become darker or lighter. I have only experienced the temporary warmth and stinging during use- no redness or anything else.
-The company also cautions those who have skin conditions or are undergoing professional cosmetic treatments such as injectable toxins like Botox or fillers- saying to check with your doctor or clinician prior to using NIRA.
-Only use on intact skin
-Don’t use if pregnant or nursing or undergoing fertility treatments
-Do not use if you have a history of skin cancer, any other cancer, or pre-malignant moles
-Do not treat if you have tanned skin which is apparently at increased risk of adverse effects with light-based devices

Overall, I’m happy with how the product functions and the ease of use. I will continue using and will update if I have any further comments or concerns. I haven’t noticed any real results yet, but I also haven’t been using it that long. One question that comes to mind is this: What is the lifespan of this device? Months? Years? Or does it give out after firing the laser a certain number of times? I could have missed it in the manual, but that is something I’m still not sure of. For the current price of $329, that is something I think people may want to know. I haven’t had any issues with the serum that comes in this package, but it seems pretty simple and basic.

Organic barbadensis leaf juice or aloe juice: as we all know that aloes have many many benefits due to its anti-inflamatory properties due to the two hormones called Auxin and Gibberellins. Organic helianthus annuus (sun flower oil): Sun flower oil is rich in Vitamin E which is a well known antioxidant for its healing properties. It also contain many great oils such as coconut, vitamin E, jojoba, rose hips, argan oil and many more which are all very healing and moisturizing for the skin

cordifolia callus culture extract (plant stem cells): Derived from Globularia Cordifolia, a species of flowering plant native to the mountains of central and southern Europe, Globularia Cordifolia Callus Culture Extract detoxifies skin by eliminating damaged proteins and other accumulated environmental wastes. It also provides protection from oxidative stress thereby reducing the effects of cell aging.

Matrixyl 3000: Matrixyl is palmitoyl-pentapeptide 3 and this is a peptide that specifically stimulates collagen synthesis and skin repair. this is a long term skin care ingredient. The two new peptides palmitoyl-tripeptide and palmitoyl-oligopeptide. They are supposed work synergistically to mimic the appearance of this broken down collagen, causing your skin to react by producing more collagen, as well as elastin. The company that owns the patent has conducted research on two panels of 23 volunteers aged from 39 to 74 to demonstrate that matrixyl 3000 is more effective than the original matrixyl at regulating skin cell activity. In early 2013 University of Reading researchers found that Matrixyl can nearly double the amount of the protein collagen needed to give skin its elasticity.

Gotu Kola: has been used to treat many conditions for thousands of years in India, China, and Indonesia. It was used to heal wounds, improve mental clarity, and treat skin conditions such as leprosy and psoriasis. Gotu kola has chemicals called triterpenoids. In animal and lab studies, these compounds seem to help heal wounds. For example, some studies suggest that triterpenoids strengthen the skin, boost antioxidants in wounds, and increase blood supply to the area. Based on these findings, gotu kola has been applied to the skin, or used topically, for minor burns, psoriasis, preventing scars after surgery, and preventing or reducing stretch marks.

I’m rating this product four stars. I think quality wise it’s slightly above average. The first thing I want to point out is how sharp it is; this is why I’m rating it four stars. The razor is pretty efficient because of its sharpness. My husband felt as though he passed the razor less times on his face; he said the razor was more precise when shaving. I’ll provide additional pictures of the product so you can see what comes in the box. The box comes with instructions, blades, a razor cover, a razor handle, and a small shaving gel. I also liked the razor cover. Most razor covers are all enclosed they will cause the razor itself to not air out and eventually rust; this cover also clips so you’re safe from accidentally cutting yourself. Overall, the biggest reason why I gave four stars was because of the sharpness. However, there are some downsides. In my opinion, the downside to the razor’s sharpness is it can be a hazard if you’re not careful. The blades we received were extremely sharp we had to be extra cautious. We normally buy very average razors. Second, this razor did not seem to provide a smooth experience like others for sensitive skin…at least for us. I believe it only has one moisture strip whereas other razors we’ve tried have more. Furthermore, the small shaving gel provided definitely feels natural; it’s not as thick or foamy as other gels or creams out there. You may have to use your own gel or cream because the one provided in the box is very light. You also need to be cautious when connecting the blade to the handle; we had a difficult time until we finally figured it out. Lastly, we had mixed feelings about the handle…but it certainly adds weight and provides durability which is a plus. All in all, I do recommend the product.

For the price, this is an excellent basic electric toothbrush and flosser. The two pieces lack the fancy features of more expensive pieces, but my dentist says all those extra features are not worth the money. The toothbrush works great and the only feature my dentist recommends is the 2 minute timer to make sure you give yourself enough time to brush all your teeth. I've always used string floss in the past, but this water flosser seems to work just as well most of the time. Sometimes there is some food stuck in my teeth that I still have to use the string for.

As I said, features are minimal. There is 1 charger for both devices, so you can't use the charger as a stand for both items. Instead of all the cardboard in the box, why not include a cheap plastic tray or stand? There also is no travel case, just a little cover for the toothbrush head. I would really prefer a full length hard case to be included instead of having to buy an aftermarket case that doesn't fit well. Also, you only get one tip each for both the flosser and the toothbrush and there is nowhere to easily store extras. This kit is probably designed for single people only, not couples or families.

Some quick thoughts on this model specifically:
* Removes smaller hairs (0.5mm) than older models, so you can be more aggressive as stray hairs start to grow back
* The "massagers" on the epilation head really do help
* You can use it dry or completely-wet, but not damp (e.g., right after the shower won't work)... and I must say that using it under running water dramatically reduces any discomfort, although it's a bit harder to notice stray hairs
* You can't use it while plugged in (that would be a serious safety hazard in the shower!) but it means that whenever the battery eventually stops holding a charge, you'll have to toss the unit)
* I wish this included a trimming head like other models, for the cases when you have longer hairs you want to attack (they have to be 7 mm or shorter before this will really pull them out)
* This doesn't include an attachment for facial hair like some do (which is OK)... just make sure that your epilator is clean if you're going to use it on your face, because otherwise it will make you break out
* The small spotlight on the unit makes it much easier to see hairs you may have missed
* The exfoliating brush is a nice touch, because epilating frequently leads to ingrown hairs. It says to use it a day or two before epilating, and it's super-gentle... almost feels like it's not doing anything, but I found it's more effective and more comfortable (if more slow) than just using a loofah. The "wait 2 days" advice is good because otherwise your skin gets sensitive

And some thoughts on epilation in general:
* This seems obvious, but I have to say it: it only hurts when a hair is being removed. This means that the first time you epilate, it's very uncomfortable. But since only a small percentage of the hair grows back before you epilate again (assuming you do it at least once every 3 months!), the subsequent touch-ups really aren't bad at all, especially on your legs. (Underarms are less comfortable, and bikini area even less so. Face is also quite sensitive, though that probably varies by person, depending on how much tweezing you normally do.)
* The first time you epilate, your legs will be unbelievably smooth. But hair grows back at different rates, so after a month or so of epilating (maybe one time each week), you'll have tiny hairs here and there, that are starting to grow back but are still too small to get. It's less of an issue with this epilator than others, and the hairs aren't really visible. So if you think someone's going to be touching your legs, then shave :-D but otherwise life is much easier if you just epilate once a week or so. Then if you don't bother doing anything for a month or so, you'll have a few stray hairs here and there, but nothing like someone who shaves regularly and then skips a month (or even a week... or even 3 days). Visible stubble is entirely a thing of the past.
* Remember that the exfoliation is important to prevent ingrown hairs (just little bumps on your legs--mine don't turn red). But if you wax, or if you age ;) you'll have to do that anyway. And this unit's exfoliator is more gentle than a loofah
* And how could I forget the #1 reason to epilate: no more underarm bumps. You know, the ones that you ALWAYS have, despite a million products on the market that say they'll banish them but don't? Sometimes when you epilate, your skin will be red for 30-90 seconds afterward, but then it fades. So NO MORE BUMPS. That alone is reason enough to own an epilator, IMO :) This also helps with bikini-area bumps, but I find in those cases that the redness can take several hours to fade, so it's fantastic to use the day before swimming but would not be a good choice immediately before pool time

First the good…
I love the razor! It’s cute and comfortable to hold. The razor has 5 blades that are stainless steel. It says they’re made of high quality steel in the USA. The razor head is magnetic so it just clicks right on, I was a little worried with it being magnetic that it might slide or move during use, but the magnets are strong and I wouldn’t even know they were attached magnetically has I not done it myself 😂 It has a metal handle that’s comfortable to hold. There’s a nice ceramic base for it to sit in when you’re not using it. The razor head moves nicely to conform to your body as you shave. It says it goes down 15 degrees and up 65 degrees (it says degrees Celsius in the image but that’s only for temp, not angles so not sure why they added the C? 😂). It has aloe on top AND bottom for extra protection and slip, which is nice. It said it came with 2 replacement razors, which I thought meant it came with the main one and then 2 additional ones, making 3, but it only comes with 2.

Now for the bad…
They recommend to replace the blades every 2 months. But how?! There’s no replacement heads here on Amazon. Why sell something on here that requires replacement heads but not sell the replacement heads on here? Hopefully they will add them before I need them because I love the razor. The razor is currently $11.99. For that you get the razor handle part, ceramic stand, and 2 razor heads. So, if I replace the razor head every 2 months like they recommend, I’ll get 4 months of use out of this. Do I want to spend $11.99 every 4 months just to get replacement heads? That is $5.99 per replacement head if that’s all I’m buying it for. Then I also get a ceramic base every time that I won’t need since I’ll already have one and another razor handle, which I guess isn’t a big deal to replace over time. I can get 4 Venus Gillette replacement heads here on Amazon for $10.99. It’s basically the same thing but I can actually buy a replacement head for it.

So, I’m not sure about this. I love the razor, but it isn’t anything crazy special. The Venus Gillette ones I usually use have aloe on them and 5 blades that work well. I don’t get the nice ceramic base for it to sit in, but that’s not a huge deal to me. I can at least replace the heads easily with it. So, it’s up to you if you don’t mind spending the $11.99 to get replacement heads for this and having to get the handle and base every time too. It’s a really nice razor that works well and is comfortable to hold, and it has a nice base to sit in. The only downside is the replacement heads. Like I said, hopefully they’ll add the replacement heads onto Amazon soon. Right now, I’d say it’s a great razor and if you don’t mind that you can’t buy replacement heads for it, I’d recommend it. If you do mind that you can’t get replacement heads for it, I’d still say it’s a great razor so maybe by the time you’re reading this they have added the replacement heads onto Amazon, so you can check and see! If they have, I’d recommend it. If not, I’d say skip them if it’s an issue not being able to buy just the replacement heads.

Great price and great shave soap. Seems to be lasting forever. Super sensitive skin used to always get bumps but discovered tallow and bought this on a budget, pretty much same quality shave. Everyone reccommends a certain $40 razor butthe best one I have had is the dirt cheap Viking Jr butterfly top. Bought because I couldnt afford expensive razors and it is the best shave with great construction compared to cheaper brands butterfly razors. It's not about spending money for a a good shave, it's about the right equipement. I finally got a good brush and stand too because the one I got years ago on here was STILL losing hairs. What a difference. Better lather, better shave, and I just wish I could afford the Proraso pre shave, never tried aftershave but seems like another money pit just like $50 razors or the expensive soaps that do the same thing. I'll try Taylor of bond street some day but I don't trust reviews anymore. I need a fatty shave soap for my skin, last I used theHare brand with Tallow and it was great. This was cheaper I think but also great. I use blades once or twice an recycle, but Astra is nice and getting super cheap. Would never pay for Feather but maybe they are better, I just want a good cheap reliable shave.
Been using safety razors since like 2014 and took my until recently to realize:
1)Fat based creams are best for my skin, I thought I was just destined to get red bumps on my neck forever but they do not happen now.

2) Preshave is more important than post shave, I started wth tallow soap so IDK what made the difference but cheap preshave makes my face feel great after shaving.

3) more$$ doesnt mean better razor or better shave soap. Reviews clear indication: Viking sells so many expensive razors but I will never buy another again after the $17 one. People say 34C or whatever is best first razor, but nope I am fine with my less aggressive cheap, well built razor. My last/first one cost$50 and the threads wore out. No thanks.

4) IDK figure out yourself. Crazy my shave is PERFECT with tallow, wool fat, fat fat fat. I used water based brands before and INSTANT improvement when I used tallow. This stuff is just as good and will buy again for the price (seems to last forever too). I will buy this exact one when I run out most likely

5) spend more if you want, but dont expect a better shave. When I have money again I will buy 3 Viking Jr razors in case I break or lose mine, some may disagree but no matter what FIND WHAT WORKS

6) Also, the shave bowl, stand, and brush make a difference, wish I knew how HORRIBLE my brush and set up was. I had a wood stand that would leave stains and couldnt handle getting wet. This time I bought a brush+stand combo and both are fantastic. After 6+ years of finding hairs in my soap from old brush I found a few at the start (they all lose a couple) then haven't had to pull hairs out since. I think it's synthetic badger too, but works great. Or maybe my old one was synthetic. IDK but this about the wool fat and this was a great buy with my little metal shave bowl (also cheap and IMO good investment and looks nice)

But yeah this is some good shave soap! Coming from a picky shaver. Crazy how I spend less money and get a better shave... seriously better stock up on those viking razors because I tried other brand butterflys, they worked but were cheaply constructed and the Viking is perfection. I thought butterfly=bad. And expensive crap = good. Wool fat puck fit perfectly in my cheap stainless bowl, get a bowl, try something like this (vegans try with some oil to replace tallow/fat) and try other stuff too. Just dont think that you need that one super expensive brand and 10 products for a good shave.

You have to know what this is before jumping in. I did but had still never done it or gotten one, and I find that whisking it is the only way to mix it right; not with a spatula, or a with a fork or spoon. I don't think it matters temperature of water as long as it's not too hot, just make sure to steam first or you can microwave some water in a bowl for 30 sec and put the towel on your face (if not too hot!!!) and then use the rest of the water for the mix. Add equal parts water and powder, I find its best to use the whole package for one mask or else I have to end up making more, but if you're experienced you will have a better time. Wait a couple minutes and then use a face spatula or fingers or w/e and paste it on your face, you can even put it on your eyes and mouth but I haven't done that completely yet. Just make sure it's AT LEAST like runny honey, it may run at first but it should leave residue- scoop/pat that stuff up every couple strokes to keep the application kinda even. Make sure there are no holes and then lie down or position in some way where your face is flattish  (you can use a pillow, don't hurt yourself). As it dries, I have experienced some minor holes, maybe because it was too thin? But it's super easy to just use your fingers and mush it back together. Leave it on for like an hour, or two, or just 30 min.  Some people say put a serum on first, to lock in the treatment with the mask; some experience a bad reaction, potentially mixing incompatible ingredients. So just aim for what you know, this mask is an amazing experience just the way it is. It's tricky and SUPER MESSY (only deduction) but when I took it off my jaw literally dropped. I never believe reviewers when I read that but I swear it. Of course, the effects were gone by the next day, but I've only done it successfully twice. If it's going on clumpy, it is not going to be even close to the same result, you need to whisk that baby. Hope this helps.

What a great idea! I used suggestions from reviewer “mom of 4” with some exceptions. I did not use any OPI branded products to prep my nails. OPI nas 99 is just 99% isopropyl alcohol so I just used that. MUCH cheaper! (Buy it at the dollar store!) I also used Gelish PH Bond Prep as that is what I had.

I watched some You Tube vids before applying the nail guards. I saw that most of the posters used some kind of tool to press down the nail guards and later discovered a silicone nail tool was what I saw; I almost bought one but ended up with really good results using the eraser end of a new pencil. Now, don’t despair if you don’t apply the nail guards perfectly! Mine were rather wrinkledy but the wrinkles were covered by the builder gel. I also found the guards wrinkled much less when I applied them from the cuticle end and put some traction on the tip end, pulling the guard down over my fingertip gluing to my finger skin before filing the excess. Make sure you file DOWN and not across to remove the excess nail guard. That’s a mistake I made when I first applied these. Don’t worry if you mess up the application of these guards. A few times I had to remove the guard just placed as I completely trashed it on the application. I found that instead of breaking into another card, I could just use two smaller guards to completely cover my billboard-sized nails.

While searching nail videos, I stumbled on Liz at The Nail Hub. If you have not seen her videos, do yourself a favor and watch some. She showed a “pushing” technique in which the gel is laid down on the middle of the nail then pushed towards the cuticle end and sidewalls of the nail, flattening the nail brush. I tried this and it resulted in a much thinner amount of product in those areas with a more natural looking nail at the end.

I used In.Hype Camouflage Pink UV Builder Gel rather than the OPI branded product (it was half the cost) laying down two very thin coats and curing each coat for 90 seconds. Then I applied two coats of my color – curing each for 60 seconds. I’m currently in love with Allenbelle chameleon thermic color 5738, a light pink to dark pink temperature changing glitter polish. I then used one coat of Gelish Top It Off as that is what I had, curing for 90 seconds. My manicure lasts perfectly for two weeks which is about as long as I can stand it before the grow-out starts to bug me. When I’m ready to redo my manicure I just pry the polish off with the paddle end of an orange stick dipped in polish remover. The polish pops right off with absolutely NO damage to my natural nails! The popped off polish looks like a press-on nail!

I applied gel nail polish for years but got tired of the soaking and scraping technique to get the polish off, which also damaged my nail beds. So I went back to regular nail polish for a few years. This wasn’t really a fix, as a regular polish manicure lasts less than a week for me before the polish chips or I just peel it off. Now I can have a long-lasting mani that doesn’t ruin my natural nails! YAY for nail guards!

My hair is fine in texture, prone to greasiness, and a bit damaged from coloring and styling (dry, brittle, breaks easily). I have gone through so many different hair products in the last couple of years, looking for something that works well for my hair type and texture. Verb Ghost shampoo and conditioner are far and away the best products I've tried. Within just a few days, my hair was softer, smoother, and healthier-feeling. After a few weeks of use, it still feels and looks terrific.

Both the shampoo and conditioner are very light, yet surprisingly effective. The shampoo has a good, cleansing lather but doesn't feel drying. The conditioner is nice and light, and doesn't leave a greasy film on my hair. I shampoo, rinse, apply the conditioner, and let sit for a couple of minutes before rinsing. Normally, my hair will feel very heavy and difficult to rinse when I leave conditioner on for that long, but this rinses out cleanly yet still feels soft and well conditioned. You also need a surprisingly small amount of product -- they are super effective. My hair is definitely clean all day and doesn't get greasy by nighttime; the next morning, it's often still clean enough that I can throw it in a bun until the afternoon before really feeling the need to wash it again. I am also shedding far less hair with each wash than I have in years.

I would think that the ionic ceramic feature could be achieved without the red light (this is a gimmick, for sure). My Goody Heat flash had the same features (ionic, ceramic, tourmaline) and did not have any lights. After continued use, I think my Goody was better at drying my hair faster at a lower setting. I got these for making my own deodorant because I'm tired of ones that don't work or have toxic fillers. It's very simple to do with some Coconut Oil, Bees Wax, Baking Soda and Essetial Oil. Just google and you can find many great recipes.

These are quality deodarant cases. The thickness of the walls is on the thin side, so it will hurt if you don't roll up the deodorant high enough and rub the thin edges on your bare skin. The roll mechanism works well. The one significant advantage I found in these when compared to others, is that you pour through the bottom. Most cases you must pour through the top and it has its problems. If your mix is very liquid, it can come spilling through the bottom, as well as sealing the moving mechanism tight. Having this unit upside down and pouring through the bottom makes for a more professional finished product. The top of the deodorant fills the cap below and takes it shape. When you open the hardened deodorant, it has the desired domed shape. Also you control how much you pour from the bottom, filing to the point where it doesn't effect the spinning mechanism.

Overall there are more expensive cases you can get that have a thicker wall, which will be more comfortable to the skin. However for this price point, these cases are the best as you can pour from the bottom.

This is a review of 1B/8A/22 (dark black going to 8ash with 22 medium blonde mix)

This hair provides hard to achieve drama, going from deep dark brown/black to a lighter shade, without ANY brassiness. This is nearly impossible to achieve on real hair (without ruining the cuticle), yet they did it and the hair appears HEALTHY.

The hair also appears relatively thick on the ends, unlike another recent purchase I made.

NOTE: Sadly, I might be returning this, so I did not disassemble the hair pieces from the package or even try these on (because another reader might receive my return). Right now, I'm undecided.

Defining color over the internet is difficult The ends are supposed to be #22 with 8A. In the picture, it looks like a light blonde of 8.5 or even maybe a 9. I decided to roll the dice in hopes that the picture would be more accurate than the description. Upon receipt, this is a medium blonde that even leans a bit dark blonde...perhaps a level 7.5 at the lightest last few inches.

If you apply it while your hair is damp, work it around and then you can then style with a brush and hair dryer to great affect. Depending on your style or hair type you can ensure the look with a lesser amount of hairspray due to the overall hold of Difi.
I have very fine hair, so this is a fantastic product for me, since I can make my hair look thicker than it is. Lol

I wash and gently towel dry my hair, then spray this on my damp hair.
I then blow dry my hair, straightening it as I dry.
Then I "lightly" spray this on my hair prior to using my flat iron.
I have then protected my hair before the heat of the dryer, and then again before the heat of the flat iron.

These ﻿Klavuu Quick Cleansing Pads do a fantastic job removing my face makeup and leave my dry and sensitive skin feeling hydrated, soft and calm. The pads are large and soaked in a generous amount of solution. My pads look totally covered in makeup after gently wiping my face to remove my makeup, so I feel they do an excellent job. There’s no fragrance, but this has a nice light scent that hints of citrus.

I squeeze out excess solution when I use the pads to remove my eye makeup (concealer, highlighter, shadow, etc.) and the pads do a great job with my eye makeup too. However, I don’t wear waterproof mascara and also don’t rub mascara off my eyes with any remover. My mascara largely comes off when I wash my face, and I’m wed to particular mascara remover that I use to wipe mascara residue after I’ve cleansed. But this works well too.

There’s no need to rinse or cleanse after I wipe my face with these pads, and I have skipped cleansing at times. This makes my dry skin feel soft and hydrated and leaves just a hint of residue that I’d guess is glycerin (but I’m not sure). Other times, I basically double cleanse given how I remove my mascara and sometimes I just really want to make sure and remove all residue from my face (especially if I’ve worn more makeup) before applying other products like an essence, serums and creams.

I’m impressed that this works so well and also has low risk ingredients. It lacks chemical fragrance, alcohol, silicones and parabens, and it has sodium hyaluronate to hydrate and plump the skin and other dry skin ingredients, such as glycerin, matricaria flower/stem extract and butylene glycol. This has other good stuff like a marine complex, botanical extracts, collagen, pearl extract and more. Love it. 5 stars.

Before I begin I should say that our family is in the process of switching our food and product choices to natural alternatives. This is the third Baja Baby product I have purchased and I'm definitely satisfied. Highly recommend this product to everyone but especially for people who suffer from skin issues.

First the good news...

This razor is much better than the reflex action. It is almost as good as a real blade but still not quite. I believe it may be the only head design that good on
the market which is why I rated it 5 stars.

Now the not so good news...

I bought it as a gold box special. If you pay full price you may need a second job
for the privilege of shaving! It feels mucho cheesey when compared with the older
razors. The design is attractive and flashy but it is over designed to the point
that it is actually less convenient to use. My example would be that you must open
each head individually to clean it and I wonder how many times this can be done before one of the heads breaks off.

My advice is to keep and eye out for a deal or wait until your old reliable shaver
fails and then bite the bullet. I am use to Norelco gouging me on the price of the
heads but now they are gouging on the price of the razor as well. When buying remember it is the type of head the razor uses that matters. The flashy crap just gives them an excuse to further increase their profit margin.
